docs.title: fd07_calls_returns: Calls and Returns
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd07_calls_returns is the FD-7 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Each of 8 passes makes nested calls, a recursion four calls deep from one call site, and a coroutine switch by two return-calls. The return address stack (RAS) pushes and pops at p2, compresses the recursion into a count on one entry, and supplies return targets. The run passes if a retired return took its correct target from the RAS, a recursion count above 1 was seen, and a p2 RETURN_CALL operation occurred.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd07_calls_returns: PASS, returns predicted by the RAS 64, p2 pushes 85,
    p2 pops 125, p2 return-calls 16, highest recursion count 4, cyc 694

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd07_calls_returns.svh, task prog_fd07 (line 23). Function addresses from the source (RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000): f1 0x8000_0500, f2 0x8000_0600, f 0x8000_0800, B 0x8000_0A00. The loop top is 0x8000_0008. One pass:

main   mixed(2); jal x1,f1              call
f1     mixed(2); jal x1,f2              call (nested)
f2     mixed(2); ret                    return to f1
f1     mixed(1); ret                    return to main
main   mixed(1); jal x1,f               call from main
f+0    mixed(2)                         6 bytes
f+6    bne x6,x0,f+16                   taken only at the bottom (n == 0)
f+10   jal x1,f                         recursive call, link f+14
f+14   c.addi                           after each recursive return
f+16   ret                              5 returns per pass
main   mixed(1)
L      jal x5,B                         call through x5, link L+4
B      mixed(2)
B1     jalr x1,0(x5)                    RETURN_CALL: to L+4, link B1+4
L+4    mixed(2)                         "A"
A1     jalr x5,0(x1)                    RETURN_CALL: to B1+4, link A1+4
B1+4   mixed(2)
B2     jalr x0,0(x5)                    RETURN: to A1+4
A1+4   mixed(1); bne x6,x0,top          back edge, taken on passes 0..6
  • Branch types are the writer's (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh): jal with rd x1 or x5 is DIRECT_CALL (lines 273 and 274); jalr_to (line 389) types a jalr by the RAS hint rule: rd and rs1 both link and unequal is RETURN_CALL, rd link a call, rs1 link a return.
  • Per pass the program retires 8 direct calls (f1, f2, f, f four times, B), 8 returns (f2, f1, f five times, B2) and 2 return-calls (derived from the source). Eight passes give 80 retired calls plus return-calls, and 80 retired returns plus return-calls.
  • emit_rec (fe_tb_writer.svh:556) writes the recursion; emit_nest (line 543) the nesting.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
The RAS is rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ras.sv.

  1. Push and pop at p2. A slot of the p2 group is presented to the RAS when it holds a branch of a valid block and no earlier slot of the block is taken (w_ras_pred_val_p2 in rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv:1090). The RAS pushes the fall-through on a call and pops on a return; a RETURN_CALL pops and then pushes (ras.sv:24-27, ras.sv:253-255).
  2. Recursion compression. The p2 push is made with recursion allowed (st_push(..., 1'b1), ras.sv:705). When the pushed address equals the current top, the top entry's count spec_rctr is incremented and TOSR does not move (ras.sv:413-421); a pop of an entry with a non-zero count decrements the count and leaves TOSR (st_retract, ras.sv:334-343). The recursive call at f+10 always pushes f+14, so every recursive call after the first matches the top.
  3. Return targets. At p1 a uBTB slot of type RETURN or RETURN_CALL with a valid top of stack takes the RAS address and pred_src = PRED_RAS (bp_cluster.sv:839-844). At p2 a return slot takes w_ras_pop_addr_p2 and PRED_RAS when the pop is valid (bp_cluster.sv:1164-1169).
  4. The commit stack. Retired calls and returns update a separate commit stack (csp, commit_top_addr; ras.sv header, lines 18-21), the fallback for a pop of an empty speculative stack.

From the run (out/fd07_calls_returns/fd07_calls_returns.fst, u_ras.spec_rctr): the count of entry 1 reads 1 from cyc 131, 2 from 133, 3 from 135 and 4 from 137, one step every two cycles, and holds 4 until cyc 374; entry 4 does the same from cyc 267 (4 at 273) and holds 4 until cyc 405. Four later episodes reach 3: entry 3 at cyc 392 to 400, entry 2 at 525 to 533, entry 9 at 581 to 589 and entry 0 at 637 to 645. In four short ones (entries 11, 12, 10 and 11, from cyc 325 to 477) the count reaches 1 and returns to 0 within six cycles.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
At retirement (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:306-310):

n_ras_ret_ok   a retired RETURN or RETURN_CALL whose FTQ entry's final
               slot at its position is valid, has pred_src == PRED_RAS,
               is taken, and has the expected target

Every cycle at p2 (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:464-487), summed over the slots:

n_ras_push     w_ras_pred_val_p2[s] with w_br_type_p2[s] a call
               (DIRECT_CALL, INDIRECT_CALL, RETURN_CALL)
n_ras_pop      w_ras_pred_val_p2[s] with RETURN or RETURN_CALL
n_rc_p2        w_ras_pred_val_p2[s] with RETURN_CALL
max_rctr       the highest u_ras.spec_rctr[i] over all entries

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:79) is n_ras_ret_ok > 0 && max_rctr > 1 && n_rc_p2 > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv:160 also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• returns predicted by the RAS counts retired returns, at most 80 here (section 1). 64 had their target from the RAS in the entry's final slot.
  • p2 pushes, pops and return-calls count p2 operations presented to the RAS, not retired instructions. w_ras_pred_val_p2 is not gated by the squash (ras_p2_keep, bp_cluster.sv:1394-1395 and line 2027), so operations of blocks squashed in the same cycle and of predicted paths later redirected are included, and an operation is missing for a call or return the p2 group did not hold (before the FTB learned it). Pops (125) exceed the 80 retired returns plus return-calls; pushes (85) exceed the 80 retired calls plus return-calls.
  • The sums are per slot (DOC-002). On the one-slot model a cycle holds at most one RAS operation.
  • highest recursion count 4. On the correct path the program's recursion gives 3: four recursive calls give one allocation and three increments. 4 is reached in the first two episodes of section 2; the four later episodes reach 3. The source of the extra increment was not traced. On the two-slot model the same program reaches 10 (DOC-007 run).
  • Departures from FD-7 in planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md: the spec's "a tail return-call" is built as a coroutine switch by two RETURN_CALLs (jalr x1,0(x5) and jalr x5,0(x1)), not a tail call. The proof adds n_rc_p2 > 0 to the spec's two conditions.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd07_calls_returns.sucl, which make view S=fd07_calls_returns opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • u_ras.tosr, tosw, bos: TOSR and TOSW step on each push, TOSR follows the link on a pop.
  • u_ras.spec_rctr.[i] and spec_ret_addr.[i] (entries 0-3 in the command file): the count of entry 1 rising to 4 at cyc 131 to 137.
  • w_br_type_p2.[0] RETURN_CALL with w_ras_pred_val_p2.[0]: the coroutine switches.
  • bpu_slot_p2.[0].pred_src PRED_RAS on return slots.
  • ras_commit group: ras_commit_val, csp, commit_top_addr change as calls and returns retire.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 40 first RAS commit (w_ras_commit_val): a retired call reaches the commit stack 128 first RAS push at p2: a call presented to the w_ras_pred_val_p2 RAS 131 entry 1's recursion count reads 1 (spec_rctr.[1]): the first compressed recursive call 137 entry 1's count reaches 4, one step every two cycles 162 first return predicted from the RAS at p2: pred_src PRED_RAS, accepted by the FTQ 256 first RETURN_CALL at p2, presented to the RAS coroutine switch 694 the run ends

docs.title: fd08_indirect: Indirect Jump
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd08_indirect is the FD-8 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Each of 40 passes runs an indirect jump and an indirect call whose targets alternate between two addresses from pass to pass. Each is preceded by a conditional whose direction alternates with it, so global history tells the two cases apart. The FTB holds one target per jump; ITTAGE learns both targets under their histories and supplies the right one at p2. The run passes if at least one retired indirect took its correct target from ITTAGE.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd08_indirect: PASS, indirect targets predicted by ITTAGE 50, cyc 1147

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd08_indirect.svh, task prog_fd08 (line 19). Addresses derived from the source (RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000); odd is pass number mod 2:

top = 0x8000_0008   c.addi
top+2       A:      bne x6,x0,top+8    taken when odd; skips one c.addi
top+8       J:      jalr x0,0(x7)      to ta (odd) or tb (even)
ta = 0x8000_0400    mixed(2); jal x0,jn
tb = 0x8000_0480    mixed(1); jal x0,jn
jn = 0x8000_0500    c.addi
jn+2        C:      bne x6,x0,jn+8     taken when even
jn+8        K:      jalr x1,0(x28)     call fa (odd) or fb (even)
fa = 0x8000_0600    mixed(2); ret
fb = 0x8000_0680    mixed(1); ret
jn+12               c.addi
jn+14               bne x6,x0,jn+22    taken on the last pass (exit)
jn+18               jal x0,top         back to top on passes 0..38
  • The writer decides every outcome and target (bcc, jalr_to, rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:412 and :389). jalr_to writes jalr rd, 0(rs1), the same encoding every pass (enc_jalr, line 345); the backend retires against the expected stream, so x7 and x28 are never read.
  • J is INDIRECT_NONRET (neither register a link) and K is INDIRECT_CALL (rd x1), by the type rule of jalr_to (fe_tb_writer.svh:396-401). The ret in fa and fb is a RETURN, predicted by the RAS.
  • exit_or_jal (fe_tb_writer.svh:615) writes the loop exit.
  • 40 passes give 80 retired indirects: J and K retire 40 times each, 20 times to each of their two targets (derived from the source).

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The FTB jump slot holds one target per jump (jmp.tgt, written from ftb_upd_jmp_target_u0, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ftb_cntrl.sv:553-554). A target that changes every pass is wrong at p2 whenever the FTB target is the one used.
  2. ITTAGE takes the folded global history (folded_hist, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ittage.sv:53-54). A and C alternate in step with the targets, so the history at J and at K differs between odd and even passes and the two targets fall in different entries.
  3. Allocation. A target mispredict allocates when the provider is not the last table and a candidate exists (alc_upd, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ittage_cntrl.sv:832-850); the new entry holds the resolved target.
  4. Selection at p2. For an INDIRECT_NONRET or INDIRECT_CALL slot the cluster takes the ITTAGE target when ITTAGE answered for this entry with a tagged hit (it_hit, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv:1148-1150), primary or alternate target by ittage_using_primary (lines 1151-1153), and records pred_src = PRED_ITTAGE; otherwise the FTB jump target and PRED_FTB (lines 1171-1174). ittage_hit is the primary-table hit (ittage_cntrl.sv:557).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
At retirement (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:311-316):

n_itt_ok   a retired INDIRECT_NONRET or INDIRECT_CALL whose FTQ entry's
           final slot at its position is valid, has
           pred_src == PRED_ITTAGE, is taken, and has the expected
           target

The final slot is the last group the FTQ accepted for the entry, p1 then p2 then p3 (fin_log, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:270-279).

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:83) is n_itt_ok > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv:160 also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• 50 of the 80 retired indirects had their right target from ITTAGE. The other 30 include the first executions of each, before ITTAGE has allocated; their sources were not traced one by one. On the two-slot model the same program gives 58 (DOC-007 run).
  • A target from ITTAGE that is wrong is not counted, and neither is one that reached the entry's final slot from another predictor.
  • Departure from FD-8 in planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md: the spec's program is "an indirect jump through a table with a repeating target pattern". The build has no table: an indirect jump and an indirect call whose targets alternate, each after a conditional that alternates with it (tb_fe_top indir). The proof matches the spec.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd08_indirect.sucl, which make view S=fd08_indirect opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • w_ittage_pred_rdy_p2 with w_ittage_pred_meta_p2.[0].ittage_hit set and ittage_prm_tgt (VA[40:1]) alternating between the two targets of the slot.
  • bpu_slot_p2.[0]: on the jump's slot, pred_src PRED_ITTAGE and target 0x8000_0400 / 0x8000_0480 for J, 0x8000_0600 / 0x8000_0680 for K.
  • bpu_redir_p2.[0] with w_ok_redir_p2: a p2 redirect, the p2 target differing from the block's p1 prediction.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 20 first misprediction of J; redirect to tb, pass 0, backend 0x8000_0480 260 first ITTAGE tagged hit at p2 (ittage_hit) slot 0 260 first target of K from ITTAGE: the call's slot accepted by the at p2 has pred_src PRED_ITTAGE FTQ 267 first target of J from ITTAGE: the jump's slot accepted by the at p2 has pred_src PRED_ITTAGE FTQ 1138 the loop exits: its last conditional taken on pass 39, backend the last pass, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_0516 1147 the run ends

docs.title: fd09_tage: TAGE Provider, Allocation and use_alt_on_na
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 0. Introduction
docs.text:
To reduce the volume of text the discussion below assumes a grasp of the concepts used in branch prediction and decoupled front ends. These are well-researched topics; some of the seminal papers include [1] [2] [3] [4].

Pacino terminology labels the prediction operation stages as p0/p1/etc and the branch predictor update operation stages u0/u1/etc.

examples/fe_demo/docs/demo_explainer.md describes how each scenario is built and run. This includes:

  • test program generation, known as "the program writer" below.
  • the list of instructions the testbench expects to retire
  • the modeled backend abstraction
  • the result line
  • the cycle counter cyc

The scenario is executed and the waveform viewer is opened with these commands:

cd examples/fe_demo
make fd09_tage
make view S=fd09_tage

Example console output is shown below listing the number of predictions, allocations and cycle count:

-I: fd09_tage: PASS, tagged-provider predictions 188, allocations 59,
    T0 by use_alt_on_na 22, cyc 1364

The Pacino branch predictors supports up to two predictions per fetch block. This is controlled by a compile time parameter, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1 or 2. To reduce the volume of signal data and improve clarity, this scenario uses NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

For reference there are two views of frontend structures: 

examples/fe_demo/docs/fe_block.svg   block connectivity
examples/fe_demo/docs/fe_pipe.svg    pipeline view

docs.title: 1. What the scenario shows
docs.text:
fd09_tage (FD-9) shows three behaviors of the Pacino TAGE predictor in response to FTQ prediction requests at p0 and FTQ updates at u0:

  1. a prediction supplied by a tagged table
  2. the allocation of a new tagged entry after a misprediction
  3. the use_alt_on_na mechanism handing a prediction from a weak tagged entry to the base table T0.

FD-9 runs a loop whose body contains a conditional branch with a random direction. The random direction is chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend. With the random direction the predictor cannot learn the branch behavior and therefore mispredicts often. These mispredictions result in allocations and eventual trigger of the use_alt_on_na (UAON) counter. Eventually the UAON counter causes the prediction to use the base table T0 as the prediction source.

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies statistical counts for FD-9. These are reported in the console output, shown above:

  • tagged-provider predictions
    • n_tage_prov in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh
    • TAGE predictions at p2 whose provider is a tagged table
  • allocations
    • n_tage_alc in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh
    • newly allocated tagged table entries written to the TAGE tables
  • T0 by use_alt_on_na
    • n_t0_uaon in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh
    • TAGE predictions at p2 that come from T0 because use_alt_on_na replaced the weak tagged provider.

docs.title: 2. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd09 in programs/fd09_tage.svh. The structure consists of a short prologue, a loop that runs 256 times, and a short epilogue.

The loop body holds two conditional branches. The bne branch at 0x8000_000E has a randomized direction. The bne branch at 0x8000_0016 returns to label top. This is the loop's back edge

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv), and the loop's first instruction, top, is at 0x8000_0008.

Address      Label  Instruction                Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1               ; prologue, 16b instr
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1           ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1               ; prologue, 16b

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1               ; loop body, 16b
0x8000_000A         addi   t0, t0, 1           ; loop body
0x8000_000E  B:     bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0014 ; randomized taken/not taken

0x8000_0012         c.addi a0, 1               ; executed when B is not taken

0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1               ; loop body, 16b

0x8000_0016         bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0008 ; back edge to top

0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1               ; epilogue
0x8000_001C         addi   t0, t0, 1           ; epilogue
0x8000_0020         c.addi a0, 1               ; epilogue

0x8000_0022         jal x0, 0                jump to itself, termination

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. They mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions so that neither branch is at the start of its fetch block: in the block that starts at top, B is at halfword position 3 and the back edge at position 7.

B's direction is random so that no predictor can learn it. B mispredicts often, and those mispredictions drive the TAGE allocations and the use_alt_on_na counter. The direction of each branch is chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend; the register operands play no part. B is taken on about one iteration in eight, 33 of the 256 in this run. Numbered from 0, the first taken iterations are 9, 16, 19, 22, 30 and 31. When B is taken, the c.addi at 0x8000_0012 is skipped.

The back edge is taken on iterations 0 to 254 and falls through on iteration 255. Its pattern is regular, and the predictors learn it.

docs.title: 3. Walkthrough
docs.text:
Pacino's TAGE implementation uses 5 tables, T0-T4. T0 is the base predictor which is untagged. T1 to T4 are tagged and use direction history in their access address generation and entry matching. The tagged tables use increasing number of history bits (length), 8, 13, 32 and 119, respectively.

T0 holds a 2-bit counter per entry and always produces a prediction.

A tagged table produces a prediction only when its tag matches. Each tagged entry holds a 3-bit prediction counter, CTR, which encodes a predicted direction in its MSB and a confidence value in the lower bits.

For the tagged table two predictions are possible, a 'primary' and an 'alternative' prediction. The table with the longest history that matches the tag produces the primary prediction, the next longest matching table is the alternative prediction or T0 when no other tagged table matches.

A prediction moves through four stages, p0 to p3. The FTQ presents the request at p0, and TAGE delivers its prediction at p2. p3 is used when the statistical corrector (SC) is enabled. SC is enabled in every scenario (the configuration the backend model drives, fe_tb_backend.svh); in this run it reverses TAGE's direction at p3 36 times. The monitor reads TAGE's own prediction and update signals, so SC changes none of the counts below.

Each fetch block has NUM_PRED_SLOTS prediction slots. A slot holds one conditional branch of the block, and TAGE predicts, updates and keeps its use_alt_on_na counter separately for each slot. This scenario is built with NUM_PRED_SLOTS = 1: every block has one slot, slot 0, and the per-slot TAGE signals below are indexed [0].

With one slot an FTB entry holds one branch. When the back edge first resolves in a block from top, the FTB splits the entry for top: it keeps B and ends the block at the back edge's address, 0x8000_0016 (the split at update, planning/arch/ftb_decisions.md section 3, at cyc 32). From then on the block at top ends there, and the back edge is the first branch of the next block, which starts at 0x8000_0016 and has its own FTB entry (allocated at cyc 43). After B is taken, fetch continues at 0x8000_0014; after a backend redirect for B not taken, at 0x8000_0012. The back edge is then the first branch of that block. Either way the back edge is in slot 0 of a block of its own and is predicted and trained with its own metadata. TAGE indexes its tables with the block's start address, so B's entries and the back edge's are separate. Both are in slot 0, so both train the one use_alt_on_na counter.

The back edge's first two resolutions, at cyc 21 and 32, came before the split took effect. Each was in a block whose one slot held another branch, so its TAGE update was suppressed (rsv_plc_occ, rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_resolve.sv lines 46 to 57 and 443). TAGE takes 254 updates for the back edge, one for each of its other resolutions, and 256 for B.

docs.title: 3.1 Allocation
docs.text:
TAGE trains on its own prediction, whatever direction the front end finally used. When a conditional branch resolves, the FTQ's update conversion compares the TAGE direction carried with the branch with the resolved direction, and marks a TAGE misprediction when they differ. On a TAGE misprediction, when the provider is not T4, TAGE writes a new entry for the branch in a table with a longer history than the provider's. The table was chosen when the branch was predicted: the first longer-history table whose entry at the branch's index has an aged useful counter of 0. The new entry holds the branch's tag and starts at CTR 3'b100, the weakest taken value.

T0's entries start at 2'b10, weakly taken, so until T0 has learned B, TAGE predicts B taken. The first allocation is at cyc 20, for B on iteration 0: B was not taken and T0 had predicted it taken. The allocation comes from TAGE's misprediction alone; the backend's first misprediction, at cyc 21, is the back edge's.

Over the run TAGE mispredicted B on 58 of the 256 iterations: on 31 of the 33 iterations on which B was taken, and on 27 of the 223 on which it was not. Each of the 58 wrote an allocation. TAGE mispredicted the back edge once, when it fell through on iteration 255, and that wrote the 59th allocation. The allocations by table:

             T1   T2   T3   T4   total
B            11   12   28    7      58
back edge     1    0    0    0       1

The first taken B is on iteration 9. In the waveform, the backend resolves it at cyc 72: tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is 1 and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8000_0014, B's target, because the front end fetched the fall-through. The allocation write is the next cycle, cyc 73, in the tage_update group:

  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.trx_type is 1 and tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_upd_val_u0 is 1: the TAGE tables take an update this cycle. trx_type is an encoded field, 0 for a prediction cycle and 1 for an update cycle: it is the arbiter's grant (tage_arb.sv line 76), an input of tage_cntrl.sv (line 58), and the encoding is stated at rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_structs_pkg.sv line 314;
  • tb.dut.u_ftq.u_upd_conv.lp_upd_p0.[0].pc is 0x8000_000E, B's address (the TAGE update input has no address; the update conversion forms every predictor's update from one record, and the loop predictor's copy carries it);
  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_upd_inp_u0.[0].cond_mispredict is 1 and .resolved_taken is 1; .tage_pred_meta.tage_prm_comp is 0, so T0 was the provider;
  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.u_alc_wr.[0] is 1 and tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.u_alc_comp.[0] is 1: the new entry is written into T1.

RTL: the TAGE misprediction is cond_mispredict, set in rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_upd_conv.sv line 218. The candidate table is chosen at p1 in pred_logic, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/tage_cntrl.sv lines 574 to 585. The allocation is formed by alc_upd_comb in tage_cntrl.sv line 853, signal u_alc_wr. T0's starting value is TAGE_T0_SRAM_INIT_VALUE, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_defines_pkg.sv line 418.

docs.title: 3.2 Training the use_alt_on_na counter
docs.text:
TAGE keeps a 4-bit counter, uaon, for each prediction slot. With one slot there is one counter, tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.uaon.[0]. It measures whether, when the provider's CTR is weak, the alternate has been more accurate than the provider. The rules are in planning/arch/tage_cntrl_uaon_update_rules.md: on an update whose prediction was weak, the counter increments when the provider was wrong and the alternate right, and decrements when the provider was right and the alternate wrong. It starts at 0.

uaon is updated only when both the provider and the alternate are tagged tables. When the alternate is T0, uaon is unchanged. The counter is therefore trained on predictions where two tagged tables matched. B and the back edge both update slot 0, so both could train the one counter; in this run only B's updates do. The back edge's predictions come from T0 until its single allocation on the last iteration, so none of its updates has a tagged provider.

The history leading up to B is random, so the entries allocated for B are later matched under histories they were not trained on. Those entries are still weak, at CTR 3'b011 or 3'b100, and some predict taken for a branch taken only one time in eight. The table counts the updates that had a tagged provider, a tagged alternate and a weak prediction, by the provider and alternate tables and by what the update did to uaon. It increments when the provider was wrong and the alternate right, decrements when the provider was right and the alternate wrong, and is unchanged when the two predicted the same direction.

             T2 over T1   T3 over T2   increment   decrement   unchanged
B                    16            6          13           0           9
back edge             0            0           0           0           0
The update inputs are in the tage_update group: tage_upd_inp_u0.[0].tage_pred_meta.tage_prm_comp, .tage_alt_comp, .tage_pred_weak, .tage_prm_tkn and .tage_alt_tkn under tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.

In the waveform, uaon.[0] first reads 1 at cyc 225, the cycle of B's update with provider T2, predicting taken, and alternate T1, predicting not taken, weak; B was not taken, so the provider was wrong and the alternate right. No update decrements it. It reaches 8 at cyc 441 and its highest value, 13, at cyc 1031, below the counter's maximum of 15.

RTL: the update is uaon_upd_ff in tage_cntrl.sv line 380, and the condition that both tables are tagged is at lines 383 and 384 (u_prm_tagged and u_alt_tagged, defined at lines 670 and 671).

docs.title: 3.3 T0 provides through use_alt_on_na
docs.text:
When uaon reaches 8, its top bit is set. From then on, a prediction whose provider is a tagged table with a weak CTR uses the alternate instead of the provider. When no second tagged table matched, the alternate is T0, and the prediction comes from T0.

The counter that allows T0 to provide is trained only on predictions where the alternate was a tagged table, as section 3.2 describes. It then governs predictions where the alternate is T0. This follows the update rule in tage_cntrl_uaon_update_rules.md.

In the waveform, the first prediction from T0 through use_alt_on_na is at cyc 460, in slot 0, for the block at top. In the tage_p2 group, tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_pred_meta_p2.[0].tage_prm_comp is 1 (T1 matched B) and .tage_prm_ctr is 3'b100, weak; .tage_using_primary is 0 and .tage_alt_comp is 0, so the prediction is T0's, not taken. All 22 such predictions in the run have T1 as the provider, and all are TAGE answers for the block at top. The monitor counts TAGE answers whether or not the FTQ accepts the group, so a count can include an answer for a block on a wrong path.

RTL: the selection is in pred_logic in tage_cntrl.sv: the trigger, a tagged provider with a weak CTR, at lines 529 to 533, and the choice of the alternate when the trigger is set and uaon[s][3] is 1 at line 539. The result is registered into tage_pred_meta_p2 by meta_p2_ff at line 364.

docs.title: 4. Events
docs.text: cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests readies already 0x8000_0000 the same cycle high, fast init 2 first TAGE response at p2: r_val_p2 and unused: FTB miss w_tage_pred_rdy_p2 20 first allocation write, B not taken, predicted table T1, slot 0 taken by T0 iteration 0 21 first backend misprediction, back edge; iteration 0 redirect to 0x8000_0008 32 the back edge resolved from top: the FTB entry the split for top ends at 0x8000_0016 34 first FTB hit at p2, the block at 0x8000_0008: slot 0 B, TAGE's direction first used, B predicted not pred_src taken PRED_TAGE 46 first p2 group at 0x8000_0016: the back edge slot 0 in slot 0, predicted taken by TAGE 72 first taken B resolved, a misprediction; iteration 9 redirect to 0x8000_0014 73 its allocation write table T1, slot 0 115 first prediction from a tagged table table T1, slot 0 225 uaon first increments, 0 to 1 provider T2, alternate T1 441 uaon reaches 8 slot 0 460 first prediction from T0, by use_alt_on_na provider T1, slot 0 1355 back edge falls through, a misprediction; iteration 255 redirect to 0x8000_001A 1364 the run ends

[2] Seznec, André. "Tage-sc-l branch predictors." JILP-Championship Branch Prediction. 2014.

docs.title: fd10_pd_redirect: Predecode Redirect
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd10_pd_redirect is the FD-10 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. It runs a chain of JALs to distinct blocks, three times. On the first pass neither the uBTB nor the FTB knows any of them, so each block is predicted to fall through. Predecode at F3 finds the JAL, the IFU writes the block back with a mispredict position, and the FTQ redirects fetch to the JAL's target. The run passes if at least one predecode redirect occurred without a backend redirect in the same cycle.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd10_pd_redirect: PASS, predecode redirects 14, cyc 255

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd10_pd_redirect.svh, task prog_fd10 (line 20). Addresses derived from the source (RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000):

0x8000_0000          mixed(3)
top = 0x8000_0008    c.addi
top+2                jal x0,T0
T(k) = 0x8000_0200 + k*0x60, k = 0..11:
  T(k)               mixed(2)               6 bytes
  T(k)+6             jal x0,T(k+1)          (k = 11: jal x0,top+0x100)
top+0x100 = 0x8000_0108
                     c.addi
0x8000_010A          bne x6,x0,top          taken on passes 0 and 1
0x8000_010E          mixed(3)
0x8000_0116          jal x0,0               halt (demo_go -> W.halt)
  • 13 JALs per pass: the 12 of the chain and the one to top+0x100. Each is DIRECT_UNC (rd x0; jal, rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:268).
  • Each target block is 0x60 bytes from the last, so every JAL starts a new fetch block.
  • The writer decides the back edge (bcc, fe_tb_writer.svh:412).

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. No prediction on the first pass. The uBTB and FTB are trained from resolved branches (FD-12), so before a JAL first retires the block holding it is predicted with no taken slot.
  2. F3 check M1. Predecode marks each position's control-transfer type. The first valid JAL in the block that is before the predicted taken position, or anywhere when nothing is predicted taken, sets w_mis_val at its position (w_m1_val, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_f3.sv:310-329). The writeback registers it as ifu_ftq_mis_val (ifu/rtl/ifu_wb.sv:86).
  3. The FTQ redirect. The FTQ's IFU interface raises pd_redir_val when it accepts a writeback with ifu_ftq_mis_val not already received for the entry, with the corrected successor as pd_redir_pc (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_ifu.sv:548-550). In the p0 arbiter it is arm 2, below a backend redirect and above p3 and p2 (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_npc.sv:329-337).
  4. Flush. Any redirect raises ftq_ifu_flush_val (ftq_ifu.sv:352), which drops the blocks younger than the redirected entry in the IFU, and the redirect rolls back history (rollback_val, ftq_npc.sv:399).

From the run (out/fd10_pd_redirect/fd10_pd_redirect.fst): w_pd_redir_val pulses 13 times between cycles 19 and 165, with w_pd_redir_pc the chain targets 0x8000_0200 to 0x8000_0620 in order and then 0x8000_0108. At cycle 175 it pulses for the halt's jal at 0x8000_0116, fetched past the cold back edge, as the backend raises its redirect for the back edge (bkend_ftq_redir_val, high in cycle 176, to 0x8000_0008); the counter sees both at the end of cycle 175 and does not count it. At cycle 186 it pulses for the jal at top+2, with w_pd_redir_pc 0x8000_0200. The backend redirect restarted fetch at top. The predictors have not seen this block start, since each block start has its own entry (BP-140). The jal in it is found at F3 again. The third pass has no predecode redirect.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counter is in the shared models, beside the FTQ fetch log (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_be_state.svh:74-75):

n_pd_redir   meas && u_ftq.w_pd_redir_val && !bkend_ftq_redir_val

meas is the measurement window: out of reset, the backend running and the stream not yet fully retired (fe_tb_backend.svh:416).

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:93) is n_pd_redir > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv:160 also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• 14 is the 13 JALs of the first pass and the jal at top+2 once more, in the block that starts at top after the back edge's backend redirect (cycle 186). After their first retirement from a block the uBTB and FTB predict them from that block's start, so the rest of the second pass and the third add none.
  • A predecode redirect in the same cycle as a backend redirect is lost to the backend redirect in the arbiter and is not counted (cycle 175).
  • After the run ends (cycle 255) w_pd_redir_val keeps pulsing about every 9 cycles while the front end runs on during the drain; the monitor does not count the drain.
  • Spec and build agree. FD-10's program is "a JAL in code not yet seen by the uBTB or FTB"; the build uses 13 such JALs (tb_fe_top jals) and runs them three times, so the trained passes show the same JALs predicted.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd10_pd_redirect.sucl, which make view S=fd10_pd_redirect opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • ifu_f3 group: ifu_ftq_pdwb_val with ifu_ftq_mis_val set, ifu_ftq_mis_pos the JAL's position and ifu_ftq_target its target.
  • w_pd_redir_val the same cycle, and the next ftq_pred_pc_p0 the target (bp_cluster_p0 group).
  • ftq_ifu group: ftq_ifu_flush_val with ftq_ifu_flush_idx, then ftq_ifu_req_val with ftq_ifu_start_pc the target.
  • Compare cycles 19-165 (first pass) with the second pass, where the chain's blocks are predicted taken and no writeback for them carries ifu_ftq_mis_val.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 19 first predecode redirect: the jal at top + 2, pass 0 found at F3, to T(0), 0x8000_0200 165 the 13th predecode redirect: the jal of T(11), pass 0 to 0x8000_0108 175 a predecode redirect to 0x8000_0116, the halt's not counted jal fetched past the cold back edge; the backend's redirect takes the next request, so the monitor does not count it 176 the back edge mispredicted, cold; redirect to backend 0x8000_0008 186 last predecode redirect: the jal at top + 2 pass 1, the 14th again, to 0x8000_0200, in the block that starts counted at top 246 back edge falls through, a misprediction; pass 2, backend redirect to 0x8000_010E 255 the run ends

docs.title: fd11_be_mispredict: Backend Mispredict
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd11_be_mispredict is the FD-11 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Each of 32 passes runs a conditional with a pseudo-random outcome, then a call and its return. The predictors cannot learn the conditional, so the backend resolves it against the prediction and redirects. The redirect squashes the younger FTQ entries, flushes the IFU, rolls back and corrects the global history, restores the RAS pointers from the entry's snapshot, and fetch restarts at the corrected PC. The run passes if a backend mispredict redirect is followed by a fetch that starts at the redirect PC.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd11_be_mispredict: PASS, backend mispredict redirects 21,
    fetches at the redirect address 21, history rollbacks 82, RAS restores 82,
    cyc 480

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd11_be_mispredict.svh, task prog_fd11 (line 21). Addresses derived from the source (RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000):

0x8000_0000          mixed(3)
top = 0x8000_0008    c.addi
0x8000_000A   A:     bne x6,x0,0x8000_0010   taken when the LFSR bit is 1
0x8000_000E          c.addi                  skipped when A is taken
0x8000_0010          jal x1,fn               call, link 0x8000_0014
fn = 0x8000_0400     mixed(2); ret           return to 0x8000_0014
0x8000_0014          c.addi
0x8000_0016   E:     bne x6,x0,top           back edge, passes 0..30
0x8000_001A          mixed(3)
                     jal x0,0                halt (demo_go -> W.halt)
  • A's direction is one bit of the writer's 16-bit Galois LFSR, taps 0xB400, seed 0xACE1 (lfsr_bit, rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:523). Computed outside the testbench from that seed, the 32 bits are 10000111001000110100011011011100: 15 taken, 17 not taken.
  • Each pass writes the same bytes (W.wp = top); cskip (fe_tb_writer.svh:502) writes the skipped c.addi dry when A is taken. The backend retires against the writer's expected stream, so x6 is never read.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The backend redirect. The in-order backend resolves each branch against the FTQ's prediction and on a difference raises bkend_ftq_redir_val with bkend_ftq_redir_cause RC_MISPREDICT (2'b00, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_structs_pkg.sv:126) and the correct PC.
  2. Priority. In the FTQ's p0 arbiter a backend redirect is arm 1 and outranks every BPU and predecode redirect (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_npc.sv:317-328); the next p0 request is bkend_redir_pc.
  3. Squash and flush. Every redirect raises ftq_ifu_flush_val (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_ifu.sv:352), dropping the IFU's younger blocks.
  4. History rollback and correction. A redirect with a cause other than RC_UNSPEC raises ftq_rollback_val (ftq_npc.sv:399). bp_history restores the pointer from the named entry's checkpoint; with rollback_corr set it writes the corrected outcome bits (rollback_n, rollback_tkn, rollback_pbit) and advances past them (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_history.sv:43-58).
  5. RAS restore. ras_restore_val is ftq_rollback_val (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq.sv:518): the RAS restores TOSR, TOSW and BOS from the entry's snapshot (ras_restore_snapshot, port rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ras.sv:65-72, writes lines 808-811 and 834-835). bp_cluster drops the restore when the redirect is the block's own p2 or p3 redirect (w_ras_restore_val, bp_cluster.sv:1402).

From the run (out/fd11_be_mispredict/fd11_be_mispredict.fst, bkend_ftq_redir_pc at each bkend_ftq_redir_val): 18 of the 21 redirects are A, 8 to 0x8000_0010 (taken) and 10 to 0x8000_000E (not taken); one is the return at cyc 49 (to 0x8000_0014), one the back edge at cyc 60, cold (to 0x8000_0008), and one the loop exit at cyc 471 (to 0x8000_001A). Every one has cause 0 (RC_MISPREDICT).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
Every cycle (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:488-501):

n_be_misp    bkend_ftq_redir_val with cause RC_MISPREDICT; it arms a
             wait for the next fetch, with the redirect PC
n_be_fix     the first FTQ fetch after it (ftq_ifu_req_val and
             ftq_ifu_req_rdy, no flush that cycle) whose
             ftq_ifu_start_pc is the redirect PC
n_rollback   ftq_rollback_val
n_ras_rest   ras_restore_val

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:100) is n_be_fix > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv:160 also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• 21 of 21 backend mispredicts were followed by a fetch at the corrected PC.
  • rollbacks and RAS restores are equal because the two are one net (ftq.sv:518). They count every redirect the FTQ takes with a cause, from any arm: backend, predecode, p3 and p2. So 82 includes the 21 backend redirects and 61 from the other arms. RAS restores counts ras_restore_val at the FTQ, before bp_cluster drops the restore of a block's own p2 or p3 redirect.
  • Departure from FD-11 in planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md: the spec's program is "a data-dependent branch the predictors get wrong". The build's branch has a pseudo-random outcome chosen by the writer (tb_fe_top misp_call); no data dependence is modeled. The proof matches the spec.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd11_be_mispredict.sucl, which make view S=fd11_be_mispredict opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • backend group: bkend_ftq_redir_val with bkend_ftq_redir_cause RC_MISPREDICT, bkend_ftq_redir_idx and bkend_ftq_redir_pc.
  • ftq_ifu group: ftq_ifu_flush_val the same cycle, then ftq_ifu_req_val with ftq_ifu_start_pc equal to the redirect PC.
  • bp_history_ras group: ftq_rollback_val, ftq_rollback_idx, ftq_rollback_corr, bpu_ghist_ptr stepping back, and ras_restore_val with ras_restore_snapshot.tosr, .tosw, .bos.
  • bp_cluster_p0 group: the next ftq_pred_pc_p0 is the redirect PC.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 19 first history rollback (ftq_rollback_val), a predecode with its RAS restore (ras_restore_val) redirect 20 first misprediction of A taken; redirect to pass 0, backend 0x8000_0010 49 the return mispredicted; redirect to 0x8000_0014 backend 53 fetch restarts at 0x8000_0014: the FTQ presents ftq_ifu_start_pc a block from the redirect address to the IFU 60 the back edge mispredicted, cold; redirect to backend 0x8000_0008 86 first misprediction of A not taken; redirect to backend 0x8000_000E 471 the loop exits: the back edge falls through, a pass 31, backend misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_001A 480 the run ends

docs.title: fd12_training: Predictor Training and the FTB Update Bubble
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd12_training is the FD-12 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. It runs nested counted loops whose body holds every kind of control transfer the predictors train on: conditionals, an indirect jump, an indirect call and its return. Each retired control transfer is resolved by the backend, converted by ftq_upd_conv into per-predictor updates, and presented to the cluster; each FTB update withholds one p0 request. The run passes if every predictor receives at least one update and at least one p0 request is withheld for an FTB update.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd12_training: PASS, update cycles uBTB 154, loop predictor 111, FTB 154,
    TAGE 111, SC 111, ITTAGE 28, RAS commit 28, p0 holds for an FTB update 154,
    cyc 454

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd12_training.svh, task prog_fd12. Bare M-mode, code at RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv:40). Addresses below are derived from the writer's emitters (mixed is c.addi, addi, c.addi repeating: 2, 4, 2 bytes).

0x8000_0000  mixed(4)                                     10 bytes
otop = +0x0A mixed(2)                     outer body
itop = +0x10 mixed(3)                     inner body
       +0x18 bne x6,x0,itop               inner loop branch, 6 passes
       +0x1C beq x0,x0,+0x28              always taken
       +0x28 mixed(2)
       +0x2E jalr x0,0(x7)  -> +0x6E      indirect jump
       +0x6E mixed(2)
       +0x74 jalr x1,0(x28) -> fn         indirect call
       +0x78 mixed(1)                     return lands here
       +0x7A bne x6,x0,otop               outer loop branch, 14 passes
       +0x7E mixed(3), jal x0,0           halt
fn = 0x8000_0800  mixed(3); jalr x0,0(ra) -> +0x78   return
  • The loops are built by loop_br and rep_iter (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:352, :364): the body is written once and its expected-stream entries are replicated, the last execution of each loop branch not taken.
  • rep_iter(eo, 14) replicates the outer body including the six inner passes already expanded, so the stream holds 14 x 6 inner branches.
  • jalr_to (fe_tb_writer.svh:389) types the jump by the RAS hint rules: jalr x0,0(x7) is INDIRECT_NONRET, jalr x1,0(x28) is INDIRECT_CALL; ret (:280) is RETURN.

Control transfers in the stream, per outer pass: 6 inner branches, the always-taken beq, the indirect jump, the indirect call, the return, the outer branch. Over 14 passes: 154 transfers, of which 112 conditionals (8 per pass), 28 indirect (jump and call) and 28 RAS operations (call and return). The halt (jal x0,0) is the stream's last entry; the counts below (154, not 155, for the uBTB and FTB) show that its update falls after the measurement window closes.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Resolution and conversion. ftq_upd_conv (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_upd_conv.sv) forms the per-slot uBTB, LP, TAGE, ITTAGE and SC payloads from the resolved record. A slot's predictor valids are presented only when the slot is accepted by every predictor it trains (upd_acc, lines 136-138 and 171; the handshake is described in the file header, lines 29-37).
  2. The cluster's type gate. bp_cluster classifies each update channel from its uBTB payload (upd_br_type, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv:1739-1746) and fans it out by type (fe_decisions.md 7.2):
  3. uBTB: any type but NO_BRANCH (bp_cluster.sv:1752-1753)
  4. LP: conditionals (:1678-1679)
  5. TAGE, SC: conditionals, each also gated by its queue ready, SC by sc_enable (:1798-1807)
  6. ITTAGE: INDIRECT_NONRET and INDIRECT_CALL (:1744-1746, :1801-1803)
  7. FTB: its own channel, for a branch or a jump (:1643-1644)
  8. RAS commit: DIRECT_CALL, INDIRECT_CALL, RETURN, RETURN_CALL (:1649-1653)
  9. The FTB update bubble. The FTB has one read port. When ftq_ftb_sched will issue an FTB update next cycle (issue_next, rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_ftb_sched.sv:327, wired to h3_ftb_upd at ftq.sv:493), ftq_npc holds its p0 request (hold term H3 in w_hold, ftq_npc.sv:307-309; rationale at ftq_npc.sv:132-137). One p0 request is withheld per FTB update.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:502-514, sampled every cycle while the stream is being measured (meas, rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_backend.svh:416). They read the valids after the cluster's gates.

n_upd_ubtb   per slot: w_ubtb_upd_u0[s].valid, summed over the slots
             of the cycle (DOC-002)
n_upd_lp     cycles with w_lp_upd_val_p0 != 0
n_upd_tage   cycles with w_tage_upd_val_u0 != 0
n_upd_itt    cycles with w_ittage_upd_val_u0 != 0
n_upd_sc     cycles with w_sc_upd_val_u0 != 0
n_upd_ftb    cycles with w_ftb_upd_val_u0
n_upd_ras    cycles with w_ras_commit_val
n_ftb_bub    cycles with u_ftq.u_npc.h3_ftb_upd

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:108-110) requires every one of the eight counts to be non-zero. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• The figures match the program's control transfers but for one: uBTB and FTB 154 (every transfer), LP, TAGE and SC 111 (the conditionals, less one), ITTAGE 28 (the indirect jump and call), RAS commit 28 (the call and the return). FTB update p0 holds 154: one per FTB update.
  • The conditional left out is the always-taken beq at +0x1C, resolved at cyc 168 in a block from +0x10 whose one slot holds the inner loop branch at position 4. The FTQ places its resolution in that occupied slot, whose prediction metadata describes the other branch, so the uBTB and FTB updates form and the LP, TAGE and SC updates are suppressed (item C, BP-139, rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_resolve.sv lines 46 to 57). The condition is rsv_plc_occ (line 443), which gates the updates at lines 551 to 560. It is the only such resolution in the run.
  • Except n_upd_ubtb, the counters count cycles with any slot valid, not slot updates; the result line says "update cycles" for that reason. DOC-002 changed n_upd_ubtb to sum its slots. On this model a cycle has one slot, so every count is of single-slot updates.
  • The run takes 454 cycles on this model and 459 on the two-slot model (DOC-007 run). On the two-slot model the LP, TAGE and SC counts are 112, since the beq has a slot of its own.
  • Departure from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-12: the program there is "any branch, first execution and the next"; the program as built is tb_fe_top's loops, with every update type, so that the proof can require an update at each predictor. The proof as built adds the RAS commit to the predictors FD-12 names.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd12_training.sucl, which make view S=fd12_training opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, backend, ftq_upd_conv, ftb_update, bp_cluster_p0. Look at:

  • bkend_ftq_rsv_val: a resolution from the backend.
  • w_ubtb_upd_u0.[0].valid, w_lp_upd_val_p0, w_tage_upd_val_u0, w_sc_upd_val_u0, w_ittage_upd_val_u0, w_ras_commit_val: the updates after the cluster's gates, by type.
  • ftb_upd_valid_u0 with ftb_upd_pc_u0: an FTB update; in the cycle before it u_npc.h3_ftb_upd is high, u_npc.w_hold is high and ftq_pred_val_p0 is low: the withheld p0 request.

docs.text:

docs.title: FD-13 L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
fd13_l1i: L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd13_l1i is the FD-13 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. A loop inside one 64-byte line shows L1I hits; cold lines show misses and MSHR fills; and a call into the upper half of a cold line, run after a FENCE.I, makes the IFU request one line twice while its fill is outstanding, so the second request merges onto the MSHR register already fetching it. The run passes if a hit, a miss and a merge each happen at least once. DOC-007 re-timed the program: a line of filler instructions after the FENCE.I keeps the line from being fetched, and filled, before the call that should miss on it (section 4).

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd13_l1i: PASS, L1I hits 48, L1I misses 29, merges 1, cyc 214

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd13_l1i.svh, task prog_fd13. Bare M-mode, code at RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv:40); X = 0x8000_0800. Addresses are derived from the writer's emitters.

0x8000_0000  mixed(2)                                     6 bytes
top = +0x06  mixed(6)                     16 bytes, within line 0
       +0x16 bne x6,x0,top                8 passes
then four times (it = 0..3; before it = 3 a FENCE.I at +0x2C and
mixed(FD13_FILL), +0x30 to +0x6F):
             jal x1, X+0x30               call: +0x1A, +0x20, +0x26,
                                          +0x70
X+0x30       c.addi
X+0x32       jal x0, X                    back into line X
X+0x00       mixed(2)
X+0x06       jalr x0,0(ra)                return
             mixed(1)
then mixed(3), jal x0,0                   halt, at +0x7E
  • The loop of 8 passes is 20 bytes from +0x06 to +0x1A and stays in the line 0x8000_0000: after its first fill every fetch of it hits.
  • X is a cold line. The block at X+0x30 starts in the upper half of line X (offset 0x30 of 64), so it needs lines X and X+1 (IFU-7).
  • The first three calls train the predictors on the path main -> X+0x30 -> X -> main. fence_i (fe_tb_writer.svh:673) then makes every L1I line invalid; the predictors keep what they learned.
  • FD13_FILL, 24 (programs/fd13_l1i.svh), is the number of filler instructions after the FENCE.I: 64 bytes, one line. The fourth call is then at +0x70.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Hits. L1iReadLatency is 2 (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_pkg.sv:122). A hit leaves the bank's compare stage as rsp_valid = c_hit (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_ctrl.sv:229, :255). In the run a request at cyc 35 (id 0, line 0x8000_0000, in the loop) is answered with id 0 at cyc 37.
  2. Misses. A miss is reported in the same stage, mis_valid = c_miss (l1i_ctrl.sv:230, :238), for the MSHR register allocated when the request was accepted; the fill comes from the memory port (l1i_mem_a_valid, l1i_mem_d_valid).
  3. The merge. On the fourth pass, after the FENCE.I, the run shows (cyc is tb.cyc, fe_tb_dut.svh:129):
  4. cyc 181: request id 0, line X (0x8000_0800), block at X+0x30
  5. cyc 182: request id 4, line X+1 (0x8000_0840), the same block
  6. cyc 183: request id 1, line X again, the predicted block at X, with u_mshr.mrg_hit set
  7. responses: id 0 at cyc 193, id 1 at 194, id 4 at 198. The IFU compares a block's first line only with the previous request's line (TD-IFU-8, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_fetch.sv:290); the previous request was X+1, so the block at X issues its own request. The MSHR finds a valid register for line X whose data has not arrived (e_val && !e_got, rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_mshr.sv:232-233) and sets mrg_hit (:256, a cacheable request). A merged request does not look up the arrays (l1i_mshr.sv:309-310: b_req_valid excludes mrg_hit).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:515-526, sampled every cycle while the stream is being measured (meas).

n_l1i_hit    per bank: u_l1i.b_rsp_valid[b], summed over the 2 banks
n_l1i_miss   per bank: u_l1i.b_mis_valid[b], summed over the 2 banks
n_l1i_merge  u_l1i.u_mshr.accept && u_l1i.u_mshr.mrg_hit

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:115) is n_l1i_hit > 0 && n_l1i_miss > 0 && n_l1i_merge > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• Hits and misses are bank lookups, not instructions or blocks. A block needing two lines counts two lookups; a merged request counts no lookup. Wrong-path requests inside the measured window are counted too.
  • DOC-002 changed n_l1i_hit and n_l1i_miss to sum the two banks in a cycle; before, a cycle with both banks answering counted once. A DOC-002 scratch check against an independent per-bank count found no cycle with both banks answering in this run, so the figures are unchanged.
  • The merge figure is 1: the event of section 2, step 3.
  • Why the fillers (DOC-007). The front end runs ahead of the backend, so when the FENCE.I retires the blocks after it are already being fetched. Without the fillers the fourth call follows the FENCE.I directly: predecode finds it before the invalidate, and the block at X+0x30 requests line X at cyc 152, the cycle after the invalidate is done (l1i_ifu_inv_done at 151), so the request misses and starts a fill. The restart after the FENCE.I (a backend redirect to the next instruction, cyc 154) flushes that block; the fill goes on. The restart PC, the call, starts a block the predictors have never seen, since each block start has its own entry (BP-140), so the call is found only by predecode, once the restart's own line, invalidated by the FENCE.I, has been filled: a predecode redirect at cyc 174. X has been filled by then; the fourth call's requests for X hit, and there is no merge (L1I hits 47, misses 28, merges 0, cyc 208). With 24 fillers the call is 64 bytes past the FENCE.I. The fetch that runs past the FENCE.I before the restart still reaches it: a predecode redirect to X+0x30 at cyc 149. At cyc 154 the restart flushes the block at X+0x30. That block had not yet requested X. In the DOC-007 runs the merge needs at least 12 fillers; with 0 or 6 there is none.
  • Departure from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-13: the program adds the fillers after the FENCE.I. The proof is FD-13's.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd13_l1i.sucl, which make view S=fd13_l1i opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, ftq_ifu, ifu_l1i, l1i. Look at:

  • ifu_l1i_req_val with ifu_l1i_req_paddr and ifu_l1i_req_id, and l1i_ifu_rsp_val with l1i_ifu_rsp_id two cycles later: a hit.
  • b_mis_valid, an MSHR e_val, l1i_mem_a_valid with l1i_mem_a_address, the l1i_mem_d_valid beats, e_got and b_fil_valid: a miss and its fill.
  • cyc 181 to 183: requests for X, X+1, X; mrg_hit set on the third. mrg_hit is the MSHR's match of the presented request, so it is also set in cycles with no request taken; the monitor counts it only with u_mshr.accept.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 5 first L1I miss (b_mis_valid), the cold line 0x8000_0000 26 first L1I hit (b_rsp_valid) 151 the invalidate is done (l1i_ifu_inv_done): the FENCE.I has made every line invalid 154 the restart after the FENCE.I: a backend backend redirect to 0x8000_0030, the next instruction 176 the fourth call found at F3 after the restart; the last predecode redirect to 0x8000_0830, X+0x30 183 the merge: the predicted block at X requests the one merge line X while its miss is in flight (mrg_hit) 214 the run ends

docs.title: fd14_translation: Sv39 Walk, Sv39x4 Nested Walk and Svadu CAS
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd14_translation is the FD-14 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Code runs at S-mode under satp Sv39; its code page has a leaf with A clear and menvcfg.ADUE set, so the walk sets A by compare-and-swap (Svadu). An ecall then moves execution to VS-mode (V=1, vsatp Sv39, hgatp Sv39x4), where the next fetch walks both stages. The run passes if a single-stage walk, a walk with V=1 that evaluates G-stage PTEs, and a CAS each happen at least once.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd14_translation: PASS, single-stage walks 2, two-stage walks 2,
    G-stage page table entry evaluations 21, compare-and-swaps 1, cyc 285

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd14_translation.svh, task prog_fd14. The address map constants are in tb/fe_demo_lib.svh:91-97.

setup   S-mode, satp Sv39, ASID 1, root 0x8F00_0000
        (begin_scen use_sv39 = 1; fe_tb_backend.svh:576-594)
        menvcfg.ADUE = 1 (csr_menv_adue, fe_tb_csr.svh:86)
        h2_tables: G-stage root 0x8E00_0000, a VS root, and page
        V 0x8005_0000 -> GPA 0x1005_0000 -> SPA 0x8160_0000
        RESET_VECTOR page mapped to itself; H mapped; C 0x8001_0000 ->
        0x8100_0000 with a leaf whose A bit is clear (PTE_LEAF & 0xBF)
0x8000_0000  mixed(3)
0x8000_0008  jal x0, C
C            mixed(8)                     22 bytes
C+0x16       ecall -> V                   to_h2: V=1 when it retires
V            mixed(8), jal x0,0           halt
  • The leaf for C is written directly with mk_pte and s_slot (fe_tb_writer.svh:735, :743): flags 0x8B (D, X, R, V; A and U clear) instead of PTE_LEAF 0xCB.
  • The regime change rides on the ecall's trap. ecall_to_vs (tb/fe_demo_lib.svh:133-136) marks the entry; when it retires, be_trap_hook (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:336-345) sets V=1, privilege S (VS), vsatp Sv39 with ASID 1 and hgatp Sv39x4 with VMID 3. The backend's trap redirect then fetches V.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Single-stage walks. The first fetch of the reset page and of C miss the ITLB and walk with V=0 (itlb_l2t_v 0). In the run: VPN 0x80000 at cyc 4, VPN 0x80010 at cyc 46 (cyc is tb.cyc, fe_tb_dut.svh:129). Each reads three PTEs from root 0x8F00_0000.
  2. The CAS. For C the leaf is valid and permitted but A is clear. The walker's leaf evaluation sets the update instead of a page fault when ADUE is set (rtl/mmu/ptw/rtl/ptw.sv:535-537; ADUE is menvcfg's for V=0, :754-756). S_S_UPD with no G-stage issues one CAS (r_m_op <= OP_CAS, ptw.sv:940-955): compare value the PTE it read, swap value the PTE with A set. In the run, at cyc 67: ptw_mem_req_op 1, ptw_mem_req_paddr 0x8F00_9080, ptw_mem_req_cmp 0x2040_008B, ptw_mem_req_swap 0x2040_00CB (A, bit 6, set; PPN 0x81000). The walk answers PPN 0x81000 at cyc 73.
  3. Nested walks. After the ecall retires, a walk with V=1 enables the G-stage when hgatp is not Bare (r_g_on, ptw.sv:752). Every VS-stage PTE address is a GPA, translated through the G-stage (S_G_START, S_G_ADDR, S_G_EVAL; states at ptw.sv:289-301), and so is the final GPA. In the run there are two V=1 walks:
  4. cyc 91, VPN 0x80010 (page C, the code after the ecall). The backend's trap redirect to V follows at cyc 92; this walk is for a fetch younger than the ecall. C is not mapped in the VS-stage, and the walk ends at cyc 168 with status ST_FAULT (ptw.sv:226) and cause 12. Nothing delivers it; the block was flushed.
  5. cyc 170, VPN 0x80050 (page V). It answers PPN 0x81600 (PA_V) at cyc 267. The first walk spends 9 cycles in S_G_EVAL, the second 12.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:527-534, sampled every cycle while the stream is being measured (meas).

n_walk_s   itlb_l2t_req_val && itlb_l2t_req_rdy && !itlb_l2t_v
n_walk_g   itlb_l2t_req_val && itlb_l2t_req_rdy &&  itlb_l2t_v
n_g_eval   cycles with u_ptw.r_st == S_G_EVAL
n_cas      ptw_mem_req_val && ptw_mem_req_rdy && ptw_mem_req_op

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:122-123) is n_walk_s > 0 && n_walk_g > 0 && n_g_eval > 0 && n_cas > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• Walks are walker requests taken, wrong path included. Of the two V=1 walks one is the flushed fetch of C described in section 2; the proof's V=1 condition would be met by either.
  • n_g_eval counts cycles in S_G_EVAL, one per G-stage PTE evaluated: 21 = 9 + 12 over the two V=1 walks.
  • The wrong-path V=1 walk occupies the walker from cyc 91 to 168, so the walk for V starts at cyc 170, about 80 cycles after the redirect. This is reported for the design owner; the demonstration does not depend on it.
  • The program is FD-14's as planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md gives it, the regime change on the ecall's trap included. The proof as built adds a G-stage evaluation count to "a walk of each kind".

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd14_translation.sucl, which make view S=fd14_translation opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, ifu_xlate, itlb, walker, walker_mem. Look at:

  • itlb_l2t_req_val with itlb_l2t_vpn and itlb_l2t_v: each walk and its kind.
  • u_ptw.r_st, shown by its state names. Before cyc 91 (V=0) the walks pass through the single-stage states (S_S_ADDR to S_S_FINAL) and the memory states (S_ISSUE to S_RSP) and through no G-stage state. From the first V=1 walk the G-stage states (S_G_START to S_G_EVAL) appear between them, and u_ptw.r_g_on is set.
  • ptw_mem_req_op 1 at cyc 67, with ptw_mem_req_cmp and ptw_mem_req_swap differing in bit 6: the CAS.
  • l2t_itlb_rsp_val with each walk's answer: l2t_itlb_status, then l2t_itlb_ppn on a hit or l2t_itlb_cause on a fault.
  • The encoded fields are shown as numbers (DOC-006):
  • l2t_itlb_status (planning/interfaces/itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md IL-4): 0 hit, 1 fault, 2 retry, 3 reserved.
  • l2t_itlb_cause, valid with a fault: the exception code of the fault, 12 instruction page fault, 20 instruction guest-page fault or 1 instruction access fault (IL-10, numbered as itlb_ifu_interfaces.md IT-6 numbers them).
  • itlb_l2t_priv (IL-3d): 0 U, 1 S; with itlb_l2t_v it is the effective privilege. 2 (reserved) and 3 (M) are never presented.
  • itlb_ifu_status (itlb_ifu_interfaces.md IT-4): 0 hit, 1 miss (a walk has started), 2 fault, 3 reserved.
  • itlb_ifu_cause (IT-6), valid with a fault: 1 instruction access fault, 12 instruction page fault, 20 instruction guest-page fault.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests S-mode, Sv39 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 4 first walk: VPN 0x80000, the reset page, single-stage (itlb_l2t_v 0) 46 walk for C: VPN 0x80010, single-stage 67 the CAS: the walker sets the A bit of C's leaf paddr 0x8F00_9080 (ptw_mem_req_op 1) 73 the walk for C answers PPN 0x81000 status 0, hit 91 first nested walk: VPN 0x80010 with itlb_l2t_v wrong path 1, for a fetch younger than the ecall 92 the ecall's trap redirect to V, 0x8005_0000 backend 168 the nested walk for C ends with a fault, cause status 1 12; nothing delivers it 170 walk for V: VPN 0x80050, nested 267 the walk for V answers PPN 0x81600 status 0, hit 285 the run ends

docs.title: fd15_faults: Page, Access and Guest-Page Fetch Faults
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd15_faults is the FD-15 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Three indirect jumps fetch from targets that fault: an unmapped page (instruction page fault), a mapped page whose physical page PMP denies execute (instruction access fault), and, after an ecall into VS-mode, a page whose VS-stage leaf names a GPA the G-stage does not map (instruction guest-page fault). Each fault travels with its block through the IFU to decode in ifu_pd_pkt_t. The run passes if each cause reaches decode on its packet with the expected cause and VA.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd15_faults: PASS, page faults at decode 1, guest-page faults at decode 1,
    access faults at decode 1, cyc 700

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd15_faults.svh, task prog_fd15. The address map is tb/fe_demo_lib.svh:91-106: C 0x8001_0000, H 0x8002_0000 (handlers hnd(k) = H + 0x40 k), V 0x8005_0000, targets tgt(k) = 0x8040_0010 + 0x20_0000 k.

setup   S-mode, satp Sv39 (begin_scen use_sv39 = 1)
        PMP: entry 2 everything RWX (pmp_all, fe_tb_csr.svh:162-165);
             entry 0 NAPOT 4 KiB at 0x8140_0000, R W, no X
             (pmp_page, fe_tb_csr.svh:155-159)
        h2_tables (fe_demo_lib.svh:123-130), V's handler page mapped
        two-stage; map_ch (fe_demo_lib.svh:110-118): reset page, C, H
0x8000_0000  mixed(3); jal x0, C
C            mixed(2)
C+0x06       jalr x0,0(x7) -> tgt(0) 0x8040_0010   nothing mapped
             -> page fault, trap to H
H            mixed(2)
H+0x06       jalr x0,0(x7) -> tgt(1) 0x8060_0010   VA -> 0x8140_0000
             -> access fault (PMP), trap to H+0x40
H+0x40       mixed(2)
H+0x46       ecall -> V                            V=1 when it retires
V            mixed(2)
V+0x06       jalr x0,0(x7) -> tgt(2) 0x8080_0010   VS leaf -> GPA
             0x2000_0000, not G-mapped
             -> guest-page fault, GPA 0x2000_0010, trap to V+0x1000
V+0x1000     mixed(4), jal x0,0                     halt
  • jr_fault and jr_gfault (fe_tb_writer.svh:707-723) emit the jalr and an expected-stream entry for the faulting fetch at the target, with its cause, its VA (fva = the target) and, for the guest-page fault, its GPA. Nothing is written at the targets.
  • The access-fault page has a valid Sv39 leaf (mk_pte with PTE_LEAF), so translation succeeds and only PMP refuses it.
  • The VS-mode switch is FD-14's: ecall_to_vs and be_trap_hook (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:336-345).

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
Each jalr is first mispredicted (no target known), so the backend redirects to the target; its fetch then faults. In the run (cyc is tb.cyc, fe_tb_dut.svh:129):

  1. Page fault. Walk for VPN 0x80400 (V=0) at cyc 90; the walker answers ST_FAULT (rtl/mmu/ptw/rtl/ptw.sv:226) cause 12 at cyc
  2. The ITLB does not install a fault; it holds it in its tracker and answers the re-request with it (rtl/mmu/itlb/rtl/itlb.sv:105-110, :525-528).
  3. Access fault. Walk for VPN 0x80600 at cyc 166 answers ST_HIT, PPN 0x81400, at cyc 187. The ITLB checks every translation with its PMP/PMA checker (pmp_pma_chk, itlb.sv:423-441, execute access, privilege S) and answers a hit that fails it as ST_FAULT with the access cause (itlb.sv:517-519). PMP entry 0 matches first and has X clear.
  4. Guest-page fault. After the ecall retires (redirect to V at cyc 202), walk for VPN 0x80800 with V=1 at cyc 399. The VS-stage leaf gives GPA 0x2000_0000, which the G-stage does not map. The walker answers ST_FAULT cause 20 (0x14) at cyc 490. A G-stage page fault is a guest-page fault (ptw.sv:79, MMU-22).
  5. Carriage to decode. The IFU's translation queue records each page's fault (xq_fault0, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_xlate.sv:316); ifu_fetch requests no line on a faulting page (ifu_fetch.sv:24, same directory); F3 assigns each position its fault, cause and VA (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_f3.sv:252-279) and writes them into the packet (fault_cause, fault_va, ifu_f3.sv:391-392). Decode sees, at pd_out[0]:
  6. cyc 108, start_pc 0x8040_0010, fault_cause IFU_FAULT_PAGE
  7. cyc 191, start_pc 0x8060_0010, fault_cause IFU_FAULT_ACCESS
  8. cyc 494, start_pc 0x8080_0010, fault_cause IFU_FAULT_GUEST_PAGE (ifu_fault_e, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_structs_pkg.sv:563-566).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from the backend's retirement hook, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:317-323, called for every retired expected entry while the stream is being measured.

n_flt_page    an expected PAGE fault entry retired with
              fault_cause == expected and fault_va == expected
n_flt_guest   the same, GUEST_PAGE
n_flt_acc     the same, ACCESS

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:129) is n_flt_page > 0 && n_flt_guest > 0 && n_flt_acc > 0. The backend also checks every retired entry against the expected stream, the guest-page fault's GPA included, and tb_fe_demo.sv requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• Each figure is 1: one faulting fetch of each kind, as the program has.
  • The walker is asked twice for each of VPN 0x80400 (cyc 90 and 107) and VPN 0x80800 (cyc 399 and 493), each time answering the fault. The run does not show which lookup starts the second walk; faults are not installed (section 2, step 1), so any later lookup of the page walks again.
  • A V=1 walk for VPN 0x80020 (page H) starts at cyc 201, the cycle before the redirect to V, for a fetch younger than the ecall; it answers a fault at cyc 278 that nothing delivers. FD-14 shows the same.
  • The program is FD-15's as planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md gives it. The proof as built also checks each packet's VA.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd15_faults.sucl, which make view S=fd15_faults opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, itlb, walker, ifu_xlate, ifu_fault, decode, backend. Look at:

  • itlb_ifu_rsp_val with itlb_ifu_status 2 (ST_FAULT, itlb.sv:239) and itlb_ifu_cause: the ITLB's fault answer.
  • l2t_itlb_status 1 with l2t_itlb_cause 12 or 20: a walk that faulted; l2t_itlb_status 0 with PPN 0x81400: the walk that succeeded before PMP refused it.
  • xq_fault0 on the translation queue entry, ifu_ftq_fault_val.
  • pd_out.[0].fault_cause and pd_out.[0].fault_va at the cycles of section 2, step 4. After each, bkend_ftq_redir_val with cause RC_TRAP to the handler.
  • The encoded fields are shown as numbers (DOC-006):
  • itlb_ifu_status (planning/interfaces/itlb_ifu_interfaces.md IT-4): 0 hit, 1 miss (a walk has started), 2 fault, 3 reserved.
  • itlb_ifu_cause (IT-6), valid with a fault: 1 instruction access fault, 12 instruction page fault, 20 instruction guest-page fault.
  • l2t_itlb_status (itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md IL-4): 0 hit, 1 fault, 2 retry, 3 reserved.
  • l2t_itlb_cause, valid with a fault: the same exception codes, for the three causes of IL-10.
  • itlb_l2t_priv (IL-3d): 0 U, 1 S; with itlb_l2t_v it is the effective privilege. 2 (reserved) and 3 (M) are never presented.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests S-mode, Sv39 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 90 walk for VPN 0x80400, the page of tgt(0), nothing mapped single-stage 104 the walker answers a page fault, cause 12 status 1 108 the page fault reaches decode: lane 0 at 0x8040_0010, fault_cause IFU_FAULT_PAGE 166 walk for VPN 0x80600, the page of tgt(1) 187 the walker answers a hit, PPN 0x81400; the status 0 ITLB's PMP check refuses it 191 the access fault reaches decode: lane 0 at 0x8060_0010, IFU_FAULT_ACCESS 202 the ecall's trap redirect to V, 0x8005_0000 backend 399 walk for VPN 0x80800, the page of tgt(2), with nested itlb_l2t_v 1 490 the walker answers cause 20, a guest-page fault: status 1 the G-stage does not map GPA 0x2000_0000 494 the third fault reaches decode: lane 0 at 0x8080_0010, IFU_FAULT_GUEST_PAGE 700 the run ends
