docs.title: FD-16 Fetch Block Crossing a Page
fd16_page_cross: A Fetch Block Crossing a Page
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd16_page_cross is the FD-16 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. A jump lands 16 bytes before the end of a 4 KiB page whose virtual successor is mapped to a non-adjacent physical page. The fetch block starting there covers both pages, so the IFU translates it twice and requests one line from each physical page; a 32-bit instruction straddles the boundary. The run passes if a translation-queue entry is popped with two translations of different PPNs.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd16_page_cross: PASS, blocks translated twice 1, cyc 112

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd16_page_cross.svh, task prog_fd16. S-mode under satp Sv39 (begin_scen use_sv39 = 1).

mapping  RESET_VECTOR page to itself
         b      = 0x8001_0000 -> 0x8100_0000
         b+4K   = 0x8001_1000 -> 0x8120_5000   not adjacent
0x8000_0000  mixed(3)
0x8000_0008  jal x0, b+0xFF0
b+0xFF0      c.addi a0,1 (7 of them)        0xFF0 to 0xFFD
b+0xFFE      addi t0,t0,1                   32-bit, bytes 0xFFE-0x1001
b+0x1002     mixed(8), jal x0,0             halt
  • map4k (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:142) writes each Sv39 leaf and records the VA page in vmap, which put_hw uses to place each halfword at its physical address, so the 32-bit instruction's two halfwords are written to different physical pages (0x8100_0FFE and 0x8120_5000).
  • The jump target is 16 bytes before the page end; FD-16 asks for a block starting within 32 bytes of it.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The block crosses. ifu_xlate marks a block as crossing when its start PC's page offset is at least CROSS_FROM 0xFE0, 32 bytes from the end (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_xlate.sv:144, :281), and then needs two lookups (r_need, :407); the queue entry keeps both pages' results (:306-308); the page-1 fields are meaningful only for a crossing block (:33-34).
  2. Two ITLB lookups and two walks. In the run (cyc is tb.cyc, fe_tb_dut.svh:129) the ITLB lookups (ifu_itlb_vpn) go from VPN 0x80010 to 0x80011, and both miss: walks for VPN 0x80010 at cyc 46 and VPN 0x80011 at cyc 70.
  3. The queue entry. At cyc 94 the entry for the block at 0x8001_0FF0 is popped with xq_cross 1, xq_ppn0 0x81000 and xq_ppn1 0x81205.
  4. Two lines from two pages. A block starting in the upper half of a line needs a second line (IFU-7), and for a crossing block that line is the second page's first line (IFU-25, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_fetch.sv:283-284). The L1I requests are 0x8100_0FC0 (cyc 93) and 0x8120_5000 (cyc 94).

The backend compares every retired instruction with the expected stream, so the 32-bit instruction at b+0xFFE retired with its expected encoding.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The count comes from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:535-539, sampled every cycle while the stream is being measured (meas).

n_xq_cross   u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_val && xq_pop && xq_cross
             && xq_ppn0 != xq_ppn1
             a translation-queue entry popped with two translations
             of different physical pages

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:133) is n_xq_cross > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors before it accepts the proof.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• The figure is 1: the program has one crossing block, and the run's translation queue shows no other entry popped with xq_cross set.
  • The monitor also requires the two PPNs to differ, so the count shows two translations, not one page's result read twice. Here they are 0x81000 and 0x81205.
  • The program meets FD-16 of planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md (a block that starts within 32 bytes of a page end); the proof is FD-16's. No departure.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd16_page_cross.sucl, which make view S=fd16_page_cross opens in Surfer. Groups: clock, ftq_ifu, ifu_xlate, itlb, ifu_l1i, decode. Look at:

  • ftq_ifu_start_pc 0x8001_0FF0: the crossing block.
  • ifu_itlb_req_val with ifu_itlb_vpn 0x80010 then 0x80011: the two lookups.
  • cyc 94: xq_pop with xq_cross 1, xq_ppn0 0x81000 and xq_ppn1 0x81205.
  • ifu_l1i_req_paddr 0x8100_0FC0 then 0x8120_5000.
  • In the itlb group the encoded fields are shown as numbers (DOC-006): itlb_ifu_status (planning/interfaces/itlb_ifu_interfaces.md IT-4) is 0 hit, 1 miss (a walk has started), 2 fault, 3 reserved; itlb_ifu_cause (IT-6), valid with a fault, is 1 instruction access fault, 12 instruction page fault, 20 instruction guest-page fault.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests S-mode, Sv39 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 46 walk for VPN 0x80010, the first page of the crossing block 70 walk for VPN 0x80011, the second page 93 L1I request for 0x8100_0FC0, the line of the first page block's start 94 the translation queue entry of the block at counted 0x8001_0FF0 popped with two translations: xq_cross 1, PPN 0x81000 and 0x81205 94 L1I request for 0x8120_5000, the second page's second page first line 112 the run ends

docs.title: fd17_rvc: Compressed and Unaligned Code
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd17_rvc is the FD-17 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Straight-line code of mixed 16- and 32-bit instructions places a 32-bit instruction at the last halfword of a 32-byte block. The IFU delivers it whole from the block's 17th halfword, and the next block starts on its tail. A loop of compressed control transfers then runs from block starts that are not 32-byte aligned. The run passes if the straddling instruction reaches retirement whole and 16-bit instructions retire.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd17_rvc: PASS, straddling 32-bit instructions delivered whole 1,
    16-bit instructions 98, cyc 198

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd17_rvc.svh, task prog_fd17. M-mode, bare. The addresses are offsets from RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000 (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_defines_pkg.sv:40). mixed(n) writes c.addi, except addi for every k with k % 3 == 1 (fe_tb_writer.svh:250; the writer is rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh).

+0x00  mixed(20)          13 c.addi, 7 addi              0x36 bytes
+0x36  4 x c.addi         to +0x3E
+0x3E  addi t0,t0,1       32-bit, halfwords +0x3E and +0x40: crosses
                          the 32-byte block end and the 64-byte line
+0x42  mixed(5)           top = +0x4E
loop, 8 passes (it = 0..7), from top = +0x4E:
+0x4E  c.addi
+0x50  c.bnez x8, +0x54   taken on odd passes (skips +0x52)
+0x52  c.addi             executed on even passes; written dry on odd
+0x54  addi
+0x58  c.jalr x1          to fn = +0x400 (INDIRECT_CALL), link +0x5A
+0x400 c.addi; addi; c.jr x1 at +0x406 (RETURN to +0x5A)
+0x5A  c.addi
+0x5C  c.j +0x64          +0x5E..+0x63 written dry (3 c.addi)
+0x64  c.addi
+0x66  c.beqz x8, top     taken on passes 0..6
+0x68  mixed(3), then jal x0,0 (halt)
  • The writer appends each compressed control transfer with its 32-bit expansion (fe_tb_writer.svh:435-492, cj, cbz, cjr, cjalr), which is what decode delivers in instr. Outcomes are the writer's, as in every scenario; x8 is not read.
  • The loop's blocks start at +0x4E, +0x54 and other non-aligned addresses: a taken transfer starts the next FTQ block at its target.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The 17-halfword window. F2 selects 17 halfwords from the block offset (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_fetch.sv:445-448), from the two lines {rd_data1, rd_data0}. A 32-bit instruction that starts at position 15 of a 32-byte block therefore completes inside the block. A block in the upper half of its line asks for the next line as well (w_two, ifu_fetch.sv:281, IFU-7).
  2. The block at +0x20 ends by falling through, and its last delivered instruction is 32-bit and starts 2 bytes before next_pc (+0x40). F3 then sets the straddle register (w_strad_set, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_f3.sv:375; the register is described at ifu_f3.sv:64) with r_strad_pc = +0x40.
  3. The block at +0x40 arrives at F3 with that start PC, so first_tail (ifu_f3.sv:250) starts its walk at position 1: the halfword at +0x40 is the tail of the instruction already delivered.
  4. Seen in the run (fst2vcd on out/fd17_rvc/fd17_rvc.fst): the FTQ blocks start at +0x00, +0x20, +0x40, ...; at cycle 21 r_strad_val is 1 with r_strad_pc 0x8000_0040; in the same cycle decode slot 4 holds start_pc 0x8000_003E, pos 15 (f), is_rvc 0, instr 0x00128293, ftq_idx 1; the next bundle starts at 0x8000_0042, pos 1, ftq_idx 2.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
Both counts are taken in be_retire_hook (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:324-329) as each expected instruction retires, while meas is set.

n_straddle   no fault, !is_rvc, pos == 15, and the packet's instr equals
             the expected (expanded) encoding: a 32-bit instruction in
             the last halfword of its block, delivered whole
n_rvc        no fault, is_rvc: a 16-bit instruction retired

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:138) is n_straddle > 0 && n_rvc > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• straddling 32-bit instructions delivered whole 1 is the instruction at +0x3E (seen at cycle 21, section 2).
  • 16-bit instructions 98 matches the program (derived from the source): 13 c.addi in mixed(20), 4 c.addi to +0x3E, 3 in mixed(5); 9 per odd pass and 10 per even pass (the c.addi at +0x52), 76 over the 8 passes; 2 in the final mixed(3). 20 + 76 + 2 = 98. The halt is 32-bit.
  • Departures from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-17:
  • FD-17's shows line names "a 34-byte block, and a 32-bit instruction straddling two blocks". These are one event here: the straddling instruction is delivered in the block before the boundary (the 34-byte window), and the next block starts on its tail. No instruction is split between two delivered blocks; the design does not do that (IFU-8, IFU-11).
  • The proof as built checks the instruction's encoding and position at retirement; FD-17's proof is "a straddling instruction delivered whole". It matches.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd17_rvc.sucl, which make view S=fd17_rvc opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • ftq_ifu_start_pc and ftq_ifu_next_pc: the blocks +0x20 to +0x40 and +0x40 to +0x60 at the start of the run.
  • ifu_ibuf_val, ifu_ibuf_en and ibuf_ifu_rdy: the blocks entering the ibuf.
  • pd_out.[4] at cycle 21: start_pc 0x8000_003E, pos 15, is_rvc 0.
  • In the loop, pd_out.[i].is_rvc set on the compressed transfers and pd_out.[0].instr holding their expansions (jal, beq/bne, jalr). The decode group shows the first lane in full and the is_rvc of every lane; of lane 4 it also shows the PC and position (DOC-006).
  • The straddle register, group ifu_f3_straddle (u_ifu.u_f3.r_strad_val, r_strad_pc, r_strad_idx): set at cycle 21 with r_strad_pc 0x8000_0040.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 21 the straddling instruction reaches decode: lane r_strad_val 4, the 32-bit addi at 0x8000_003E, position 15; the straddle register holds 0x8000_0040 22 the next bundle starts on its tail: lane 0 at 0x8000_0042, position 1 28 first fetch of fn, 0x8000_0400, after the c.jalr ftq_ifu_start_pc 198 the run ends

Run it from examples/fe_demo/: make fd17_rvc runs the scenario; make view S=fd17_rvc opens its waveform in Surfer.

docs.title: fd18_uncached: Uncached Fetch
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd18_uncached is the FD-18 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Code runs from a page whose Sv39 leaf has PBMT NC, then from one whose leaf has PBMT IO (DOC-003). The IFU fetches each one instruction per FTQ entry, each block only after every older entry has committed, with uncached L1I requests that are answered from memory and never written into the array. The run passes if the L1I takes uncached requests from each page and no line of either page is filled into the L1I.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd18_uncached: PASS, uncached requests from the NC page 28,
    from the IO page 10, uncached lines filled 0, cyc 797

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd18_uncached.svh, task prog_fd18, ported from tb_fe_top's uc_nc. S-mode under satp Sv39. The pages (map4k, and map4k_pbmt at rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh:770):

RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000 -> PA 0x8000_0000   cacheable
c            0x8001_0000 -> PA 0x8100_0000   cacheable
u            0x8001_1000 -> PA 0x8120_3000   PBMT 1 (NC)
io           0x8001_2000 -> PA 0x8120_4000   PBMT 2 (IO)

RESET  mixed(3); jal x0, c
c      mixed(4); jal x0, u+0x10
u+0x10 mixed(3)                   +0x10 +0x12 +0x16
u+0x18 bne (cskip, taken)         to +0x22; +0x1C..+0x21 written dry
u+0x22 mixed(2)                   +0x22 +0x24
u+0x28 bne (cskip, not taken)
u+0x2C c.addi
u+0x2E jal x0, u+0x200
u+0x200 mixed(2); bne x6 at +0x206 back to +0x200, 3 iterations
u+0x20A mixed(2); jal x0, c+0x200 at +0x210
c+0x200 mixed(3); jal x1, u+0x400 at c+0x208 (link c+0x20C)
u+0x400 mixed(2); ret at +0x406
c+0x20C mixed(2); jal x0, io+0x10 at c+0x212
io+0x10 mixed(3)                  +0x10 +0x12 +0x16
io+0x18 bne (cskip, taken)        to +0x22; +0x1C..+0x21 written dry
io+0x22 mixed(2); jal x0, c+0x300 at io+0x28
c+0x300 mixed(2), then jal x0,0 (halt)
  • 24 instructions execute on page u (derived from the source): 9 at u+0x10..u+0x2E, 12 at u+0x200..u+0x210, 3 at u+0x400..u+0x406. 7 execute on page io, at io+0x10..io+0x28.
  • The program records the IO page's PPN in io_ppn (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh line 160), which the monitor uses to split the uncached requests between the two pages.
  • map4k_pbmt with a non-zero PBMT also records the PA and VA pages in uc_ppn and uc_vpn (fe_tb_writer.svh:774-776), which the monitor reads.
  • The program sets the backend's eager mode (eager = 1'b1, programs/fd18_uncached.svh:31). With nothing presented, the backend then resolves a branch that ended its block against the block the FTQ fetched after it, and commits the entry of the last retired instruction (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_backend.svh:162-191).

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Uncached marking. On an ITLB hit the IFU translation queue marks the page uncached when its effective attributes are not both cacheable and idempotent (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_xlate.sv:226). The ITLB passes the leaf's PBMT to the PMA check (rtl/mmu/itlb/rtl/itlb.sv:420, :435); NC is not cacheable, and IO is neither cacheable nor idempotent. xq_uc carries the mark (ifu_xlate.sv:324).
  2. The commit gate. F0 does not match an uncached block until commit_ptr equals its FTQ index (w_uc_gate, rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_fetch.sv:278, IFU-22). Its requests carry ifu_l1i_req_uncached (ifu_fetch.sv:316).
  3. One instruction per entry. F3 delivers only the block's first valid instruction; when more would follow (w_uc_cut), it ends the block there with mis_val and ifu_ftq_uc_end, so the FTQ redirects to the next sequential instruction, a new entry (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_f3.sv:368-373, the writeback at lines 421 to 431; the rule is described at ifu_f3.sv:94-114). A JALR is delivered alone with no redirect.
  4. No allocation. An uncached lookup is a miss whatever the tags hold (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_ctrl.sv:229-230, L1I-24). A free MSHR register taken by an uncached request is marked not to allocate (e_alloc <= !req_uncached, rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_mshr.sv:486), and a fill is installed only when fil_alloc is set (l1i_mshr.sv:350-360).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:540-554, sampled every cycle while meas is set.

n_uc_req_nc  ifu_l1i_req_val && ifu_l1i_req_rdy && ifu_l1i_req_uncached,
             with the request's PA page not in io_ppn
             an uncached request the L1I took from the NC page (one per
             line requested)
n_uc_req_io  the same, with the PA page in io_ppn: from the IO page
n_uc_alloc   per bank b: u_l1i.u_mshr.b_fil_valid[b] and the filled
             line's PA page is in W.uc_ppn
             a line of an uncached page written into the array

n_uc_alloc sums the two banks of a cycle into n_ucal and adds the sum once (DOC-002; it counted a cycle with both banks once before). It is 0 in this run either way.

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:144) is n_uc_req_nc > 0 && n_uc_req_io > 0 && n_uc_alloc == 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• uncached requests from the NC page 28 counts lines requested, not instructions. From the run (fst2vcd on out/fd18_uncached/fd18_uncached.fst, requests with ifu_l1i_req_uncached taken):
  • 14 for the 9 instructions at u+0x10..u+0x2E: the 4 in the lower half of the line request PA 0x8120_3000 alone; the 5 in the upper half (u+0x22 onward) request 0x8120_3000 and 0x8120_3040 in consecutive cycles (IFU-7);
  • 11 for the 12 instructions at u+0x200..u+0x210 (line 0x8120_3200). Which instruction was served without a request of its own was not traced;
  • 3 for the 3 instructions at u+0x400 (line 0x8120_3400).
  • from the IO page 10: the 7 instructions at io+0x10..io+0x28. The 4 in the lower half of the line request PA 0x8120_4000 alone; the 3 in the upper half (io+0x22 onward) request 0x8120_4000 and 0x8120_4040 (IFU-7). The first is at cyc 647.
  • The requests are about 19 to 25 cycles apart (cycles 111, 130, 149, 168, ... in the run): each waits at F0 for the previous entry to commit.
  • uncached lines filled 0 is the proof's last term: no fill of a line of PA page 0x81203 or 0x81204.
  • FD-18 of planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md covers NC and IO (DOC-003); the program runs both. The commit gate FD-18's waveform names is w_uc_gate, in the ifu_fetch group with xq_uc.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd18_uncached.sucl, which make view S=fd18_uncached opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • u_xlate.xq_uc set for the blocks on the two uncached pages, and the commit gate u_fetch.w_uc_gate opening for each block.
  • ftq_ifu_commit_ptr reaching each uncached block's ftq_ifu_idx before its ifu_l1i_req_val with ifu_l1i_req_uncached.
  • each uncached block closing after one instruction, and the next block starting at the next instruction (ftq_ifu_start_pc). The writeback that closes it, ifu_ftq_mis_val, is not in this command file; waves/fd10_pd_redirect.sucl shows it.
  • In the l1i group: b_mis_valid for each uncached request, an MSHR e_val, l1i_mem_a_valid and l1i_mem_d_valid, and no b_fil_valid for the 0x8120_3xxx or 0x8120_4xxx lines.

docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests S-mode, Sv39 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 111 first uncached request: the first block on page NC page u asks the L1I for line 0x8120_3000 (ifu_l1i_req_uncached) 126 first uncached block closed after one instruction: F3 ends it (ifu_ftq_uc_end), and the next entry starts at the next instruction 306 first request for 0x8120_3200, the loop at NC page u+0x200 555 first request for 0x8120_3400, the function at NC page u+0x400 647 first uncached request from the IO page, line IO page 0x8120_4000 772 last uncached request the 38th 797 the run ends

docs.title: fd19_fencei_cbo: FENCE.I and cbo.inval
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd19_fencei_cbo is the FD-19 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. A function is called, rewritten by a store, and called again after a FENCE.I; a second function is treated the same way with a cbo.inval of its line. Each maintenance operation retires, the backend holds decode, the IFU passes the invalidate to the L1I, the L1I drains and clears, the IFU acknowledges, and the backend restarts fetch at the next instruction. The run passes if both invalidates complete and fetch restarts after each.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd19_fencei_cbo: PASS, whole-cache invalidates 1, line invalidates 1,
    invalidates done 2, maintenance acknowledgements 2,
    restarts at the next instruction 2, cyc 235

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd19_fencei_cbo.svh, task prog_fd19, with the self-modifying-code tasks smc_* (tb/fe_demo_lib.svh:148-187, after tb_fe_top's tasks of the same names). M-mode, bare. Offsets from RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000; f = +0x800, g = +0xC40. Addresses derived from the source.

+0x00  mixed(3)
+0x08  jal x1,f ; f: 6 c.addi, ret      smc_fn(f, 2): two calls
+0x0C  jal x1,f ; (the same)
+0x10  mixed(2)
+0x16  sw x0,0(a0)       smc_store(f): retiring it rewrites f as
                         3 x addi t1 and ret
+0x1A  mixed(2)
+0x20  fence.i
+0x24  mixed(2)
+0x2A  jal x1,f          smc_call_new(f): the stream expects the new
                         body (3 x addi t1, ret)
+0x2E  mixed(2)
+0x34  jal x1,g ; +0x38 jal x1,g        smc_fn(g, 2)
+0x3C  sw x0,0(a0)       smc_store(g)
+0x40  bne (cskip, taken) to +0x46; +0x44 written dry
+0x46  cbo.inval (a0)    PA 0x8000_0C64: the line of g, 0x8000_0C40
+0x4A  mixed(60)         160 bytes of code not yet fetched
+0xEA  jal x1,g          smc_call_new(g)
+0xEE  mixed(2), then jal x0,0 (halt)
  • A store's memory effect is a list of halfword patches applied when it retires (fe_tb_writer.svh:644-668; the shared models are in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/). Until then memory holds the old code, so a fetch of f or g after the store and before the maintenance operation would return the old body and the stream would not retire.
  • fence_i and cbo_inval (fe_tb_writer.svh:673-677, :698-703) mark their stream entries with maint 1 and 2; cbo.inval's entry carries the PA.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The backend. When a maintenance entry retires it stops taking decode's output (mt_pend) and raises cmt_ifu_maint_val with the operation and PA (fe_tb_backend.svh:357-365, :463-470). After ifu_cmt_maint_ack it redirects to the instruction after the operation with cause RC_REPLAY (fe_tb_backend.svh:156-161).
  2. The IFU (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_maint.sv). r_st steps I_IDLE -> I_REQ -> I_WAIT -> I_ACK (ifu_maint.sv:58-63, :87-96). I_REQ drives ifu_l1i_inv_val with ifu_l1i_inv_all for FENCE.I or the address for cbo.inval (:72-74); I_WAIT waits for l1i_ifu_inv_done and clears the IFU line buffer in that cycle (lb_clr_val, :75); I_ACK raises ifu_cmt_maint_ack for one cycle (:71).
  3. The L1I (rtl/core/frontend/icache/rtl/l1i_maint.sv). From the acceptance cycle the core port takes nothing new (hold, :73). M_DRAIN waits for !busy_any (inv_all) or !busy_line (inv_line) (:96-98), M_CLEAR applies the clear in one cycle, M_DONE raises inv_done (:75, :99-100). inv_line clears every way of the line's set (:25-27).
  4. Seen in the run (fst2vcd on out/fd19_fencei_cbo/fd19_fencei_cbo.fst):
cycle  FENCE.I                       cbo.inval
71     cmt_ifu_maint_val (op 0);     184  cmt_ifu_maint_val (op 1);
       L1I takes inv_all                  L1I takes the line,
       (mt_busy_any 0)                    mt_busy_any 1, mt_busy_line 0
72-73  M_DRAIN, M_CLEAR              185-186  M_DRAIN, M_CLEAR
74     l1i_ifu_inv_done              187  l1i_ifu_inv_done
75     ifu_cmt_maint_ack             188  ifu_cmt_maint_ack
77     redirect to +0x24, cause 2    190  redirect to +0x4A, cause 2
79     fetch starts at +0x24         192  fetch starts at +0x4A

RC_REPLAY is 2'b10 (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_structs_pkg.sv:128). The taken branch at +0x40 is resolved as a mispredict: a backend redirect to +0x46 with cause 0 at cycle 174.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:555-570, sampled every cycle while meas is set.

n_inv_all    ifu_l1i_inv_val && ifu_l1i_inv_rdy && ifu_l1i_inv_all
n_inv_line   ifu_l1i_inv_val && ifu_l1i_inv_rdy && !ifu_l1i_inv_all
n_inv_done   l1i_ifu_inv_done
n_mt_ack     ifu_cmt_maint_ack; arms mt_wait with mt_pc, the PC of
             the maintenance entry + 4
n_restart    the first fetch the FTQ presents after the ack
             (ftq_ifu_req_val && ftq_ifu_req_rdy && !ftq_ifu_flush_val)
             starts at mt_pc

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:152-153) is n_inv_all > 0 && n_inv_line > 0 && n_inv_done >= 2 && n_restart >= 2. n_mt_ack is only reported. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors, which here includes the new bodies of f and g.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• One FENCE.I, one cbo.inval: whole-cache invalidates 1, line invalidates 1, a done and an ack for each, and each followed by a fetch at the next instruction.
  • The drains had nothing to wait for. At the FENCE.I take mt_busy_any was 0. At the cbo.inval take mt_busy_any was 1 (the fills of the code after it), but inv_line waits only for busy_line, which was 0: no register held line 0x8000_0C40. So M_DRAIN lasted one cycle both times. The program's comment ("so fills are in flight when the L1I takes the invalidate") holds for mt_busy_any; it does not make the line drain wait.
  • Departures from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-19:
  • FD-19's program is "code modified then FENCE.I; a cbo.inval of a code line". The program does both, and also reruns the modified code, so the stream check shows each invalidate took effect.
  • FD-19's proof is "the invalidate completes and fetch restarts". The proof as built asks for both kinds, two dones and two restarts at the next instruction. It is stronger.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd19_fencei_cbo.sucl, which make view S=fd19_fencei_cbo opens in Surfer. Look at, around cycles 71-79 and 184-192:

  • cmt_ifu_maint_val, cmt_ifu_maint_op (0 FENCE.I, 1 cbo.inval) and cmt_ifu_maint_paddr.
  • the IFU's u_maint.r_st stepping from I_REQ to I_ACK, and ifu_l1i_inv_val with ifu_l1i_inv_rdy. ifu_l1i_inv_all is set for the FENCE.I; ifu_l1i_inv_paddr names the cbo.inval's line.
  • mt_busy_any, l1i_ifu_inv_done, ifu_cmt_maint_ack.
  • bkend_ftq_redir_val with bkend_ftq_redir_cause RC_REPLAY, then ftq_ifu_req_val with ftq_ifu_start_pc at the next instruction.
  • mt_busy_line, which decides the cbo.inval drain, and the L1I's u_maint.r_st (M_DRAIN, M_CLEAR, M_DONE), both in the maintenance group.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 71 the FENCE.I reaches the L1I: it takes the mt_busy_any 0 invalidate of every line (ifu_l1i_inv_all) 74 first invalidate done (l1i_ifu_inv_done) after M_DRAIN, M_CLEAR 75 first maintenance acknowledgement (ifu_cmt_maint_ack) 77 the restart after the FENCE.I: a backend backend redirect to 0x8000_0024, cause RC_REPLAY 79 fetch starts at 0x8000_0024, the next ftq_ifu_start_pc instruction 174 the branch at 0x8000_0040 mispredicted; redirect backend to 0x8000_0046, the cbo.inval 184 the cbo.inval reaches the L1I: it takes the mt_busy_line 0 invalidate of line 0x8000_0C40 187 second invalidate done 188 second maintenance acknowledgement 190 the restart after the cbo.inval: a backend backend redirect to 0x8000_004A, cause RC_REPLAY 192 fetch starts at 0x8000_004A, the next instruction 235 the run ends

Run it from examples/fe_demo/: make fd19_fencei_cbo runs the scenario; make view S=fd19_fencei_cbo opens its waveform in Surfer.

docs.title: fd20_backpressure: Backpressure
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd20_backpressure is the FD-20 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. The backend takes decode's output one cycle in four. Decode stalls first, the ibuf fills and refuses the IFU, the IFU stops draining the FTQ, the FTQ fills, and the FTQ stops issuing p0 requests. The run passes if each of the four stalls occurs.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd20_backpressure: PASS, stall cycles with the instruction buffer full 378,
    FTQ full 324, decode held 368, no p0 request 331, cyc 537

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd20_backpressure.svh, task prog_fd20. M-mode, bare. Offsets from RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000.

+0x00  mixed(3)
top = +0x08
       mixed(23)          15 c.addi and 8 addi, 62 bytes
top+62 bne x6,x0,top      taken on passes 0..38, 40 passes
       mixed(3), then jal x0,0 (halt)
  • be_rdy_pat = 4 (programs/fd20_backpressure.svh:24, FD-U2): the backend drives dec_ibuf_rdy only in cycles with cyc % 4 == 0 (rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_backend.svh:463-465).
  • The stream is 3 + 40 x 24 + 3 = 966 instructions plus the halt (derived from the source).

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. Decode. With dec_ibuf_rdy low three cycles in four, the ibuf's read port presents a bundle that is not taken.
  2. The ibuf. Its ready is registered occupancy: ibuf_ifu_rdy is high while r_count <= DEPTH - FTQ_PD_WIDTH (rtl/core/frontend/ibuf/rtl/ibuf.sv:114). DEPTH is 64 (ibuf.sv:57; fe_top instantiates it without an override, rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/rtl/fe_top.sv:802) and FTQ_PD_WIDTH 16 (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_defines_pkg.sv:237), so it refuses above 48 slots.
  3. The IFU. F3 holds its block, payload and all, while ibuf_ifu_rdy is low (rtl/core/frontend/ifu/rtl/ifu_f3.sv:56-57, IB-7). Fetch and retirement slow to the backend's rate while p0 keeps allocating, so the FTQ fills.
  4. The FTQ. ftq_full is set when the age of alloc_ptr over commit_ptr reaches FTQ_ALLOC_LIMIT (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_ptr.sv:247), which is FTQ_DEPTH, 64 (ftq_ptr.sv:196, bp_defines_pkg.sv:30). It is hold condition H2 of ftq_npc: w_hold includes h2_ftq_full (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_npc.sv:306-309) and ftq_pred_val_p0 = ~w_hold (ftq_npc.sv:377).
  5. Seen in the run (fst2vcd on out/fd20_backpressure/fd20_backpressure.fst): the first cycle with pd_out[0].valid and dec_ibuf_rdy low is 18; the first ifu_ibuf_val with ibuf_ifu_rdy low is 71, with u_ibuf.r_count 52; the first ftq_full is 138 (tb.cyc values).

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:571-576, sampled every cycle while meas is set. All four are counts of CYCLES in which the condition holds, not of stall events.

n_ibuf_full  ifu_ibuf_val && !ibuf_ifu_rdy   the IFU offers, the ibuf
                                             refuses
n_ftq_full   ftq_full                        (tb's ftq_full, fe_top's
                                             port, fe_tb_dut.svh:98,
                                             :101)
n_dec_stall  pd_out[0].valid && !dec_ibuf_rdy
n_p0_held    !ftq_pred_val_p0                for any hold reason

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:160-161) is that each count is above zero. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors.

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• cyc 537 is the measured window, so the stall counts are fractions of it: the ibuf refuses the IFU in 378 of 537 cycles, the FTQ is full in 324, decode holds a bundle in 368.
  • no p0 request 331 counts every hold, not only backpressure. From the run: of the 331 cycles, 324 have ftq_full and 7 have u_ftq.u_npc.h3_ftb_upd (the FTB update hold, H3) without it.
  • The order of onset (18, 71, 138) is the propagation from decode back to the FTQ; the counts alone do not show it.
  • Departures from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-20:
  • FD-20's program is "a long run with the backend accepting slowly"; the program fixes the rate at one cycle in four (be_rdy_pat 4, FD-U2 closed).
  • FD-20's proof is "each stall occurs". The proof as built also counts n_p0_held, which includes the FTB update holds; it does not separate the p0 stall caused by the full FTQ. n_ftq_full is the count of that cause.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd20_backpressure.sucl, which make view S=fd20_backpressure opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • decode group: dec_ibuf_rdy high one cycle in four and pd_out.[0].valid held, from cycle 18.
  • ibuf group: ifu_ibuf_val with ibuf_ifu_rdy low from cycle 71; u_ibuf.w_n_pres and w_n_pop, the slots presented and taken.
  • ftq group: ftq_full from cycle 138, with w_commit_ptr, ftq_pred_idx_p0 and ftq_ifu_idx.
  • bp_cluster_p0 group: ftq_pred_val_p0 low while ftq_full is set; u_npc.w_hold high with it.
  • u_ibuf.r_count in the ibuf group, the occupancy the ready is computed from: 52 at cyc 71, when ibuf_ifu_rdy first refuses.

docs.title: 6. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 18 decode first holds a bundle: pd_out.[0].valid decode stall with dec_ibuf_rdy low 71 the instruction buffer first refuses the IFU: buffer full ifu_ibuf_val with ibuf_ifu_rdy low, r_count 52 138 the FTQ first full (ftq_full); the p0 request FTQ full is withheld 526 back edge falls through, a misprediction; pass 39, backend redirect to 0x8000_004A 537 the run ends

docs.title: fd21_commit: Commit
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

fd21_commit is the FD-21 demonstration scenario. It is a demo, not a verification test. Calls and returns retire in order. The backend's retirement watermark moves the FTQ commit pointer one entry per cycle, and each committed entry whose prediction block ends in a call or a return pushes or pops the RAS commit stack. The run passes if the commit pointer moves in at least 16 cycles and the commit stack changes.

The scenario runs on the one-slot model (Makefile SCEN_2S, DOC-006). A recorded run:

-I: fd21_commit: PASS, cycles the commit pointer moved 42,
    cycles the RAS commit stack changed 36, cyc 214

docs.title: 1. The program
docs.text:
Source: programs/fd21_commit.svh, task prog_fd21, ported from tb_fe_top's calls. M-mode, bare. Offsets from RESET_VECTOR 0x8000_0000; f = +0x800, g = +0xA00, h = +0xC00. Addresses derived from the source.

+0x00  mixed(3)
top = +0x08
+0x08  10 x c.addi
+0x1C  jal x1,f            main calls f (link +0x20)
f+0x00 mixed(3); 10 x c.addi
f+0x1C jal x1,g            f calls g (link f+0x20)
g      mixed(2); ret       g returns
f+0x20 c.addi; 13 x c.addi
f+0x3C jal x1,h            f calls h (link f+0x40)
h      mixed(2); ret       h returns
f+0x40 c.addi
f+0x42 ret                 f returns to main
+0x20  c.addi
+0x22  bne x6,x0,top       loop_br; rep_iter: 6 passes, the last not
                           taken
+0x26  mixed(3), then jal x0,0 (halt)
  • Each pass makes three calls and three returns; the deepest point is main -> f -> g (or h), two return addresses on the stack.
  • loop_br and rep_iter (fe_tb_writer.svh:352-383, in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/) write the body once and append its other five executions to the expected stream.

docs.title: 2. Why the program produces the behavior
docs.text:
1. The watermark. The backend raises bkend_ftq_commit_val with bkend_ftq_commit_idx the newest FTQ entry all of whose instructions have retired: when the first instruction of a new entry retires, the watermark becomes the entry before it (track_entry, fe_tb_backend.svh:70-93; driven at :458-459 when the resolution queue is empty).
  2. The commit walk. ftq_commit frees every entry from commit_ptr to the watermark, ONE ENTRY PER CYCLE because the RAS commit port is scalar (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_commit.sv:26-31): commit_step_val (:235) advances commit_ptr by one (:252). w_commit_ptr in ftq.sv is that pointer.
  3. The RAS commit. The committing entry's taken call, return or return-call slot sets ras_commit_val and ras_commit_br_type (rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_entry.sv:275-285). In the RAS a pop moves csp down and a push writes commit_ret_addr and moves csp up (c_pop, c_push, c_nxt, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ras.sv:749-759; registered at :844-848). commit_top_addr is the entry below csp (ras.sv:185-187).
  4. Seen in the run (fst2vcd on out/fd21_commit/fd21_commit.fst, while meas is set): w_commit_ptr changes in 42 cycles; ras_commit_val is high in 36 cycles, 18 with ras_commit_br_type DIRECT_CALL and 18 with RETURN; csp reaches 2.

docs.title: 3. What the monitor counts
docs.text:
The counts come from tb/fe_demo_mon.svh:577-582, sampled every cycle while meas is set. Both are counts of CYCLES.

n_commit_adv  u_ftq.w_commit_ptr differs from its value the cycle
              before (pv_commit)
n_csp_chg     u_bpu.u_ras.csp or u_ras.commit_top_addr differs from
              the cycle before (pv_csp, pv_ctop)

pv_commit, pv_csp and pv_ctop are updated every cycle, inside or outside the measured window (fe_demo_mon.svh:639-641).

The proof (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh:167) is n_commit_adv >= 16 && n_csp_chg > 0. tb_fe_demo.sv also requires the whole stream to retire with no errors, and the backend checks every RAS commit against the retired call or return (the RAS commit check, fe_tb_backend.svh:391-415).

docs.title: 4. Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• cycles the commit pointer moved 42: since the walk frees one entry per cycle, this is also the number of FTQ entries committed inside the measured window.
  • cycles the RAS commit stack changed 36 is 3 calls and 3 returns times 6 passes (derived from the source; the run shows 36 RAS commits, section 2). Each operation changes csp in its own cycle.
  • Departures from planning/showcase/fe_demo_scenarios.md FD-21:
  • FD-21's proof is "commits advance; the commit stack changes". The proof as built sets a floor of 16 cycles for the first; the number is the testbench's, not FD-21's.

docs.title: 5. Waveform
docs.text:
The saved view is waves/fd21_commit.sucl, which make view S=fd21_commit opens in Surfer. Look at:

  • backend group: bkend_ftq_commit_val and bkend_ftq_commit_idx, the watermark.
  • ftq group: w_commit_ptr stepping by one per cycle up to the watermark.
  • ras_commit group: ras_commit_val with ras_commit_br_type DIRECT_CALL or RETURN and ras_commit_ret_addr; u_ras.csp moving between 0 and 2; commit_top_valid and commit_top_addr (+0x20, f+0x20, f+0x40).
  • ras group: the speculative pointers tosr and tosw, which move at prediction time, ahead of the commit stack.

docs.title: fd22_sc_slot1: SC Reversing Slot 1
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. What the scenario shows
docs.text:
fd22_sc_slot1 is the FD-22 scenario of the front-end demonstration. One fetch block holds two conditional branches. TAGE predicts both at p2, one in each prediction slot. At p3 the statistical corrector (SC) reverses the direction of the second, in slot 1, and the cluster redirects the request stream from slot 1. FD-5 (docs/fd05_p3_override.md) shows the same reversal in slot 0 on the one-slot model; this scenario needs the second slot and runs on the two-slot model (SCEN_2S in the Makefile). demo_explainer.md describes how a scenario is built and run, and defines the terms used here.

When the scenario passes, it prints one line. This is the line from a run on 2026-10-19, the run the cyc values below come from:

-I: fd22_sc_slot1: PASS,
    p3 redirects from slot 1 reversed by SC behind a TAGE slot 0 8,
    from slot 0 reversed by SC 1, cyc 368

The monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 583 to 601, counts a p3 redirect the FTQ accepted (tb.dut.u_ftq.w_ok_redir_p3) for the block at p3 when one of the slots raised it:

  • p3 redirects from slot 1 reversed by SC behind a TAGE slot 0, the monitor variable n_sc_s1: slot 1 raises the redirect, slot 1 is a conditional whose pred_src is PRED_SC, and slot 0 is a conditional whose pred_src is PRED_TAGE;
  • from slot 0 reversed by SC, n_sc_s0: slot 0 raises the redirect and its pred_src is PRED_SC.

The scenario passes when the first count is greater than zero (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh line 173) and every instruction the testbench expects retires without error. The second count is reported for information only. On the one-slot model the first count is 0, because there is no slot 1, and the scenario fails. The run took 368 cycles.

docs.title: 2. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd22 in programs/fd22_sc_slot1.svh. Between a short prologue and epilogue it runs a loop of 48 passes. The loop's first block holds two conditional branches: A, never taken, and B, taken on the odd passes. The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. It starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv). The loop's first instruction, top, is at 0x8000_0008.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0002         addi t0, t0, 1           prologue filler
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             loop body filler
0x8000_000A         addi t0, t0, 1           loop body filler
0x8000_000E  A:     bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0014  never taken
0x8000_0012         c.addi a0, 1             always executed
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             loop body filler
0x8000_0016  B:     bne x6, x0, 0x8000_001C  taken on odd passes
0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1             executed when B is not
                                             taken
0x8000_001C         c.addi a0, 1             B's target; filler
0x8000_001E         addi t0, t0, 1           filler
0x8000_0022         c.addi a0, 1             filler
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1             filler
0x8000_0026         addi t0, t0, 1           filler
0x8000_002A         c.addi a0, 1             filler
0x8000_002C         bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0008  back edge to top
0x8000_0030         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_0032         addi t0, t0, 1           epilogue filler
0x8000_0036         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_0038         jal x0, 0                jump to itself; the run
                                             ends here

In the block that starts at top, A is at halfword position 3 and B at position 7. The filler after B moves the back edge into the next block, so the block at top holds exactly the two conditionals. B skips one instruction: its target, 0x8000_001C, lies inside the block, so the block's successor differs between B taken and B not taken.

The program writer writes the loop body once per pass at the same addresses, so the code in memory does not change; the passes differ only in the expected list (demo_explainer.md sections 2 and 3). When B is taken, W.cskip in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh writes the c.addi at 0x8000_001A in dry mode, and the expected list leaves it out. The backend model resolves each branch with the direction the program recorded; x6 is never read.

docs.title: 3.1 Two conditionals in one prediction block
docs.text:
The FTB records, for a block start address, up to NUM_PRED_SLOTS branches, each with its position. On the two-slot model the block at top has A in its first conditional field and B in its second. At p2 the cluster presents them in slots 0 and 1 (p2_class_comb, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv lines 1010 to 1046). For each conditional slot, TAGE's direction is used when TAGE answered for the block (w_taken_p2, lines 1032 to 1036). The slot's pred_src is then PRED_TAGE (lines 1161 and 1162).

In the waveform, the first p2 group for the block at top with both slots valid is at cyc 45, in the bp_cluster_p2 group. tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[0] is A at pos 3 and tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[1] is B at pos 7. Both are COND with pred_src PRED_TAGE; A is predicted not taken and B taken.

RTL: the placement of the FTB's conditional fields into slots is in p2_class_comb, bp_cluster.sv lines 1010 to 1046.

docs.title: 3.2 SC answers at p3 for each slot
docs.text:
SC answers one cycle after TAGE, at p3, separately for each slot. For a conditional slot with an SC hit, and no loop predictor direction at p2, the p3 direction is SC's (w_taken_p3, bp_cluster.sv lines 1301 to 1304). When it differs from the p2 direction, the p3 slot records pred_src PRED_SC (p3_slot_comb, lines 1340 to 1352).

The successors at p3 are chained from the highest slot down, as at p2: slot 1's successor is B's target when B is taken and the block's fall-through when it is not, and slot 0's successor is A's target or slot 1's successor. A slot redirects when it is reachable and its p3 successor differs from its p2 successor (lines 1307 to 1325). Because A is not taken, slot 1 is reachable, and a reversal of B changes both successors: slot 1 and slot 0 raise the redirect together, to the same address. The FTQ accepts it (ok_redir_p3, rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_shadow.sv lines 220 and 221) and the next request starts there (arm 3 of ftq_npc.sv, line 338). The block at top has its own FTB entry, which ends one block above its start, so its fall-through is 0x8000_0028.

In the waveform, the first redirect from slot 1 is at cyc 110. One cycle earlier, at p2, the tage_p2 group shows tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_pred_meta_p2.[1].tage_prm_comp 0 (T0 is the provider) with .tage_pred_tkn 0, so slot 1 is predicted not taken. At cyc 110, in the sc_p3 group, tb.dut.u_bpu.w_sc_hit_p3.[1] is 1 and tb.dut.u_bpu.w_taken_p3.[1] is 1: SC predicts B taken. In the bp_cluster_p3 group tb.dut.bpu_slot_p3.[1].pred_src is PRED_SC. Both tb.dut.bpu_redir_p3.[1].valid and .[0].valid are 1, with target_pc 0x8000_001C, B's target.

At cyc 114, TAGE's provider for slot 1 is T1 with CTR 3'b100, weakly taken (tage_prm_comp 1, tage_prm_ctr 3'b100 at cyc 113); SC predicts not taken, and the redirect is to 0x8000_0028, the block's fall-through.

docs.title: 3.3 The reversals in the run
docs.text:
There are 9 p3 redirects in the run, all for the block at top:

cyc                         slot   p2 direction   p3 direction   target
46                          0      not taken      taken          0x8000_0014
110                         1      not taken      taken          0x8000_001C
114, 130, 136, 280, 303,    1      taken          not taken      0x8000_0028
326, 349

The reversal of slot 0 is early in the run, while SC is still learning: it reverses A, which is never taken, and the backend corrects it (a redirect to 0x8000_0012 at cyc 56). The backend's last misprediction of B is at cyc 204 (a redirect to 0x8000_001A). After it, each of SC's four reversals of B replaces a wrong TAGE direction with the right one, so none is followed by a backend redirect.

RTL: the SC hit for slot s is w_sc_hit_p3[s], bp_cluster.sv lines 1296 and 1297; the monitor counts are n_sc_s1 and n_sc_s0 in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 589 to 600.

docs.title: 4. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 22 first backend misprediction, the back edge; pass 0 redirect to 0x8000_0008 45 first p2 group for the block at top with both A slot 0, B slots: A and B, pred_src PRED_TAGE slot 1 46 first p3 redirect: SC reverses A in slot 0 to 0x8000_0014 56 A mispredicted; redirect to 0x8000_0012 backend 110 first p3 redirect from slot 1: SC reverses B to 0x8000_001C from not taken to taken 114 SC corrects TAGE's taken for B, provider T1 to 0x8000_0028 204 last backend misprediction of B; redirect to backend 0x8000_001A 358 back edge falls through, a misprediction; pass 47 redirect to 0x8000_0030 368 the run ends

docs.title: FD-23 A Jump Behind Two Conditionals
fd23_jump_cut: A Jump Behind Two Conditionals
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. What the scenario shows
docs.text:
fd23_jump_cut is the FD-23 scenario of the front-end demonstration. A fetch block holds two conditional branches followed by a jump. With two prediction slots an FTB entry holds at most two branches, so when the jump resolves in that block the FTB splits the entry: it keeps the two conditionals and ends the block at the jump's address (planning/arch/ftb_decisions.md section 3, BP-140). When both conditionals are predicted not taken, the block ends at the jump by the FTB's own stored end, and the next block, which starts at the jump, predicts the jump in slot 0. The scenario runs on the two-slot model (SCEN_2S in the Makefile). demo_explainer.md describes how a scenario is built and run, and defines the terms used here.

DOC-006 wrote this scenario for the cluster's cut (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md section 10, BP-138 and BP-139), which ended such a block at the jump when the FTB entry held all three branches. Since BP-140 no entry the FTB writes holds a branch that no slot carries, the cut does not fire, and DOC-007 re-pointed the scenario at the split.

When the scenario passes, it prints one line. This is the line from a run on 2026-10-19, the run the cyc values below come from:

-I: fd23_jump_cut: PASS, blocks the FTB ends at the jump 23,
    the jump predicted in slot 0 of the next block 21,
    blocks cut by the cluster 0, cyc 244

The monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 602 to 628, counts in the p2 groups the FTQ accepted (tb.dut.u_ftq.w_ok_slot_p2):

  • blocks the FTB ends at the jump, the monitor variable n_jmp_end: a group whose two slots are conditionals predicted not taken, whose block end, tb.dut.bpu_blk_pft_p2, is the jump's address, and in which the cluster's cut, tb.dut.u_bpu.w_cut_p2, is clear. The jump's address is the testbench variable jmp_pc (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh line 153). The program sets it when it writes the jump, so the end is checked against the program;
  • the jump predicted in slot 0 of the next block, n_jmp_next: the next accepted group whose block starts at that address, tb.dut.u_bpu.r_pc_p2, with a jump in slot 0 at position 0, predicted taken;
  • blocks cut by the cluster, n_cut: accepted groups with w_cut_p2 set, reported for information.

The scenario passes when the first two counts are greater than zero (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh line 180) and every instruction the testbench expects retires without error. On the one-slot model the counts are 0 and the scenario fails. The run took 244 cycles.

docs.title: 2. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd23 in programs/fd23_jump_cut.svh. Between a short prologue and epilogue it runs a loop of 24 passes. The loop's first block holds the conditionals C1 and C2, never taken, followed by the jump J to a block at 0x8000_0400 that holds the back edge. The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. It starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv). The loop's first instruction, top, is at 0x8000_0008.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0002         addi t0, t0, 1           prologue filler
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             loop body filler
0x8000_000A  C1:    bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0010  never taken
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1             always executed
0x8000_0010  C2:    bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0016  never taken
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             always executed
0x8000_0016  J:     jal x0, 0x8000_0400      the jump
0x8000_0400         c.addi a0, 1             filler
0x8000_0402         addi t0, t0, 1           filler
0x8000_0406         bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0008  back edge to top
0x8000_040A         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_040C         addi t0, t0, 1           epilogue filler
0x8000_0410         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_0412         jal x0, 0                jump to itself; the run
                                             ends here

In the block that starts at top, C1 is at halfword position 1, C2 at position 4 and J at position 7. The back edge is taken on passes 0 to 22 and falls through on pass 23. The program writer writes the loop body once per pass at the same addresses, so the code in memory does not change (demo_explainer.md, section 2); x6 is never read. Before it writes J, the program sets jmp_pc to J's address, 0x8000_0016.

docs.title: 3.1 The FTB entry for top
docs.text:
The FTB keeps one entry per block start. An update for a branch resolved in a block from that start adds the branch to the entry. When the entry already holds a branch at that position, the update changes that branch in place. The entry stores its branches in position order. An entry holds at most NUM_PRED_SLOTS branches. When an update would make it hold more, the lowest NUM_PRED_SLOTS positions are kept, the block's end becomes the address of the lowest branch not kept, and a jump not kept clears the jump field. This is the split (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ftb_cntrl.sv, THE UPDATE, lines 464 to 494; the split at lines 592 to 615). The uBTB applies the same rule (apply_upd, ubtb.sv lines 291 to 376).

C1 and C2 resolve first: at cyc 52 and 53 the FTB allocates the entry for top with C1, then adds C2. The entry ends one block above its start, at 0x8000_0028. At cyc 56 the first p2 group for top predicts both taken (TAGE's base table starts weakly taken), and the statistical corrector reverses them at p3, at cyc 57, to the block's end. J then resolves in a block from top and is the third branch: at cyc 65, in the ftb_update group, tb.dut.ftb_upd_pc_u0 is 0x8000_0008, ftb_upd_pos_u0 7, ftb_upd_is_jmp_u0 1, and tb.dut.u_bpu.u_ftb.u_ftb_cntrl.upd_split is 1 with upd_cut_pos 7. The entry keeps C1 and C2 and now ends at position 7, J's address.

docs.title: 3.2 The block ends at the jump
docs.text:
At p2 the cluster places each conditional field of the entry in its slot and the jump field in the lowest slot that holds no conditional (p2_class_comb, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv lines 1010 to 1046). The entry for top has no jump field, so the two slots hold C1 and C2. The block's fall-through, the address fetch continues at when no slot is taken, is the FTB's stored end when the FTB answered, no branch is cut and no jump is held (w_pft_p2, p2_succ_comb, lines 1133 to 1141); it leaves the cluster as bpu_blk_pft_p2 (line 1275). The cut, which would end the block at a branch the FTB reports and no slot carries (w_cut_p2, lines 1064 to 1074), stays clear.

In the waveform, the first accepted p2 group of the block at top that ends at J is at cyc 71. In the bp_cluster_p2_ftb group, tb.dut.u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0008. The FTB answer holds both conditional fields (w_ftb_br_valid_p2.[0] and .[1]) and no jump (w_ftb_jmp_valid_p2 0), w_cut_p2 is 0, and tb.dut.bpu_blk_pft_p2 is 0x8000_0016, J's address. In the bp_cluster_p2 group, tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[0] is C1 and .[1] is C2, both COND at pos 1 and 4, not taken, pred_src PRED_TAGE. The uBTB was split the same way: its p1 prediction for top, tb.dut.bpu_pred_pft_p1, is 0x8000_0016 from cyc 70, so p1 and p2 agree.

docs.title: 3.3 The next block predicts the jump
docs.text:
The next block starts at 0x8000_0016. The predictors have not seen this block start, so at first neither the uBTB nor the FTB answers for it. Fetch runs past J, and predecode at F3 finds it (predecode redirects to 0x8000_0400 at cyc 79 and 92). The update for J from that start allocates its entry at cyc 91, with J at position 0. From then on the FTB answers for 0x8000_0016 with J in its jump field, and the cluster places J in slot 0.

The first counted pair is at cyc 97 and 98. At cyc 97 the block at top ends at 0x8000_0016, as in 3.2; at cyc 98, r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0016 and tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[0] is DIRECT_UNC at pos 0, taken, with target 0x8000_0400 and pred_src PRED_FTB. The two blocks counted at cyc 71 and 84 ended at J before J's own entry existed; their next groups had no FTB answer, so the count of blocks ended at J, 23, exceeds the count of next blocks, 21.

RTL: the split is upd_split and upd_cut_pos in ftb_cntrl.sv; the block end is w_pft_p2 in bp_cluster.sv; the monitor is tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 602 to 628.

docs.title: 4. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 19 predecode redirect to 0x8000_0400: J found at pass 0 F3, not yet known to the predictors 41 first backend misprediction, the back edge; pass 0 redirect to 0x8000_0008 52 FTB entry for top allocated with C1; C2 added ftb_update at cyc 53 56 first p2 group for top: C1 and C2 in slots 0 predicted taken and 1, end 0x8000_0028 57 SC reverses both at p3; redirect to 0x8000_0028 p3 redirect 65 J resolved from top: the split, upd_split 1, upd_cut_pos 7 the entry ends at 0x8000_0016 71 first p2 group for top ending at 0x8000_0016, counted, C1 and C2 not taken, w_cut_p2 0 n_jmp_end 91 FTB entry for 0x8000_0016 allocated with J at ftb_update position 0 98 the block at 0x8000_0016 predicts J in slot 0, counted, taken, to 0x8000_0400 n_jmp_next 234 back edge falls through, a misprediction; pass 23 redirect to 0x8000_040A 244 the run ends

docs.title: fd24_call_slot1: A Call in Slot 1
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. What the scenario shows
docs.text:
fd24_call_slot1 is the FD-24 scenario of the front-end demonstration. A fetch block holds a conditional branch followed by a call. With two prediction slots the conditional is in slot 0 and the call in slot 1. When the conditional is predicted not taken, the call in slot 1 is on the predicted path, and the return address stack (RAS) pushes the call's return address at p2 from slot 1. The function's return is then predicted from the stack. The scenario runs on the two-slot model (SCEN_2S in the Makefile). demo_explainer.md describes how a scenario is built and run, and defines the terms used here.

When the scenario passes, it prints one line. This is the line from a run on 2026-10-19, the run the cyc values below come from:

-I: fd24_call_slot1: PASS,
    RAS pushes from slot 1 behind a not-taken conditional 24,
    returns predicted by the RAS 21, cyc 270

The two counts are:

  • RAS pushes from slot 1 behind a not-taken conditional, the monitor variable n_push_s1 (tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 629 to 637): p2 groups the FTQ accepted (tb.dut.u_ftq.w_ok_slot_p2) in which slot 0 is a conditional predicted not taken and slot 1, a call, is presented to the RAS (tb.dut.u_bpu.w_ras_pred_val_p2.[1]);
  • returns predicted by the RAS, n_ras_ret_ok (lines 306 to 310): a retired return whose block's final slot for it has pred_src PRED_RAS and the right target.

The scenario passes when both counts are greater than zero (tb/fe_demo_proofs.svh line 186) and every instruction the testbench expects retires without error. On the one-slot model the first count is 0 and the scenario fails. The run took 270 cycles.

docs.title: 2. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd24 in programs/fd24_call_slot1.svh. Between a short prologue and epilogue it runs a loop of 24 passes. The loop's first block holds C, a conditional that is never taken, followed by a call to the function f at 0x8000_0400. f returns to the block that holds the back edge. The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. It starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv). The loop's first instruction, top, is at 0x8000_0008.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0002         addi t0, t0, 1           prologue filler
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             prologue filler
0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             loop body filler
0x8000_000A  C:     bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0010  never taken
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1             always executed
0x8000_0010         jal x1, 0x8000_0400      the call; return address
                                             0x8000_0014
0x8000_0400  f:     c.addi a0, 1             function body
0x8000_0402         addi t0, t0, 1           function body
0x8000_0406         jalr x0, 0(x1)           return to 0x8000_0014
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             filler
0x8000_0016         addi t0, t0, 1           filler
0x8000_001A         bne x6, x0, 0x8000_0008  back edge to top
0x8000_001E         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_0020         addi t0, t0, 1           epilogue filler
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1             epilogue filler
0x8000_0026         jal x0, 0                jump to itself; the run
                                             ends here

In the block that starts at top, C is at halfword position 1 and the call at position 4. The jal with rd x1 is a call (DIRECT_CALL) and the jalr x0, 0(x1) a return (RETURN), by the program writer's types (W.jal and W.ret in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh). The back edge is taken on passes 0 to 22 and falls through on pass 23.

docs.title: 3.1 The call reaches slot 1
docs.text: The FTB entry for the block at top holds C in its first conditional field and the call in its jump field. At p2 the cluster places C in slot 0. The call goes to the lowest slot that holds no conditional, which is slot 1 (p2_class_comb in rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_cluster.sv lines 1010 to 1046, the jump at lines 1037 to 1045). A taken branch ends the block, so a slot is on the predicted path only when no earlier slot is predicted taken (w_reach_p2, lines 1076 to 1084).

docs.title: 3.2 The RAS operation of slot 1
docs.text:
At p2 a slot of a valid block is presented to the RAS when it holds a branch on the predicted path (w_ras_pred_val_p2, lines 1086 to 1091). The RAS performs the slots' operations in order, slot 0 first, so a call in slot 1 pushes its return address after slot 0's operation (rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/ras.sv lines 24 to 27). A push allocates an entry at the write pointer TOSW, and the read pointer TOSR moves to it (st_push at ras.sv lines 406 to 454; the p2 push at lines 696 to 705).

In the waveform, the first counted push is at cyc 90. It is also the first p2 group for top with both slots valid. In the bp_cluster_p2 group, tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[0] is C, a COND at pos 1, not taken, pred_src PRED_TAGE. tb.dut.bpu_slot_p2.[1] is the call, DIRECT_CALL at pos 4, taken, with target 0x8000_0400 and pred_src PRED_FTB. In the ras group tb.dut.u_bpu.w_ras_pred_val_p2.[1] is 1 with w_br_type_p2.[1] DIRECT_CALL, and w_ras_pred_val_p2.[0] is 1 for C, a conditional, which the RAS does not act on. At cyc 91 tb.dut.u_bpu.u_ras.tosr has moved from 0 to 1 and tosw from 0 to 2. spec_ret_addr.[1] holds 0x8000_0014, the call's return address.

docs.title: 3.3 The return predicted from the stack
docs.text:
The block at f holds the return. At p2 a return slot takes the RAS's pop address as its target when the pop is valid, with pred_src PRED_RAS (bp_cluster.sv lines 1164 to 1170). Of the 25 accepted p2 groups for the block at 0x8000_0400, 23 predict the return from the RAS with target 0x8000_0014. The first is at cyc 91, the cycle after the first counted push.

Before cyc 90 the call is found four times by predecode, each time in a block whose start has no FTB entry holding it yet; each block start has its own entry (BP-140). Predecode redirects to 0x8000_0400 at cyc 19 (the block at 0x8000_0000, pass 0), 60 (top, after the back edge's first backend redirect), 75 (0x8000_0010, C's target, while C is predicted taken) and 85 (0x8000_000E, C's fall-through, after the backend corrects C).

When the call and the return retire, the commit stack follows them (tb.dut.ras_commit_val with u_ras.csp). The run has 48 commits: a push and a pop for each of the 24 passes.

RTL: the slot-1 presentation is w_ras_pred_val_p2[1] in bp_cluster.sv; the monitor is tb/fe_demo_mon.svh lines 629 to 637.

docs.title: 4. Events
docs.text:
cyc Event Other 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests fast init 0x8000_0000 the same cycle 19 predecode redirect to 0x8000_0400: the call pass 0 found at F3, not yet known to the predictors 40 first return mispredicted, cold; redirect to backend 0x8000_0014 51 back edge mispredicted, cold; redirect to backend 0x8000_0008 76 C mispredicted taken; redirect to 0x8000_000E backend 90 first RAS push from slot 1, behind C not taken; counted the first p2 group for top with both slots 91 TOSR 1, TOSW 2; entry 1 holds 0x8000_0014; PRED_RAS first return predicted from the RAS 261 back edge falls through, a misprediction; pass 23 redirect to 0x8000_001E 270 the run ends

docs.title: fe_top Connectivity Inventory
docs.text:
This file records the net-level connectivity of fe_top. The block diagrams docs/fe_block.svg and docs/fe_pipe.svg use it as the reference for connections between blocks.

Section 3 lists the nets between instances, section 4 lists the fe_top boundary ports, section 6 lists the predictors inside bp_cluster, and section 7 describes the page table walker that the testbench places beside fe_top.

docs.title: 1. Notation
docs.text:
Notation:

  • W bits is the packed width. N x W bits is an unpacked array of N elements, each W bits wide.
  • from is the instance output that drives a net, and to is the instance input that reads it.
  • bind fe_top.sv:L is the line of the port connection.
  • A file name without a directory is one of the module files listed in section 2.1.

fe_top is a purely structural module containing 7 instances, 141 nets between instances (section 3) and 75 top-level ports (section 4).

4. The fe_top boundary
docs.text:
The ports are declared at fe_top.sv:96-217 and grouped as FE-17 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1378) and FE-20 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1445) group them; fe_top.sv:29-60 restates the grouping. -> is a fe_top input read by an instance input; <- is a fe_top output driven by an instance output.

FE-17 counts two groups that cross (translation and backend) and says the instruction path is not a boundary group: what crosses is the L1I's l2-side port mem, a topology edge. FE-20 adds three inward groups (csr, config, maintenance) and one outward dependency, the ibuf read ready. The RTL carries all of them as fe_top ports; the L1I's mem port is section 4.8. Two outputs are in no group (section 4.12).

bkend_ftq_redir_val is the one fe_top net with two readers: the FTQ and the ibuf clear (fe_top.sv:44-45, IBUF-13).

docs.title: 6. Inside bp_cluster
docs.text: The cluster is a four-stage pipeline (p0 to p3) with an update stage u0 and its write u1 (bp_cluster.sv:55-61). The FTQ-facing ports are grouped in the port list as follows; the predictor instances are at bp_cluster.sv:1812-2035.

docs.title: 6.1 bp_cluster port groups
docs.text:
group                                       ports at       spec
P0  prediction request, FTQ -> BPU          bp_cluster.sv:109-112
                                            ftq_bpu 3
P1  initial prediction, BPU -> FTQ          :114-123   ftq_bpu 4
RD  redirects p2, p3                        :125-131   ftq_bpu 6
SL  slot correction p2, p3                  :133-150   ftq_bpu 4a
BK  block-scalar correction p2              :152-160   ftq_bpu 4c
M2  metadata write p2 (tage ittage lp ftb)  :162-175   ftq_bpu 7.1
M3  metadata write p3 (sc)                  :177-182   ftq_bpu 7.2
UP  updates u0: ubtb lp ftb tage ittage sc  :184-224   ftq_bpu 8
RS  RAS restore, commit, flush              :226-234   ftq_bpu 8
RB  history rollback                        :236-263   ftq_bpu 9
HI  history pointer and buffer outputs      :265-271   ftq_bpu 9
CF  configuration inputs                    :273-279   FE-20 config
ST  status: init readies, queue status      :281-300   ftq_bpu 3, 8

ftq_bpu is planning/interfaces/ftq_bpu_interfaces.md.

inst           module      line  stage

u_sc           sc          1985  p3 (indexes at p2, answers at p3)

Stages are bp_cluster.sv:55-61 and the comments above each instance (bp_cluster.sv:1813, 1839, 1856, 1882, 1933, 1955, 1977, 2009). ubtb is instantiated with N_SLOTS = NUM_PRED_SLOTS (bp_cluster.sv:1844-1846).

docs.title: 7. The walker beside fe_top in the testbench
docs.text:
fe_top has no walker; the testbench instantiates one beside it (FE-17 translation, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1391; MMU-1a). The shared model rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_dut.svh holds both, included in module tb by examples/fe_demo/tb/tb_fe_demo.sv:57 and by tb_fe_top.

fe_top dut (.*)     fe_tb_dut.svh:101  every fe_top port, by name, to
                                       the tb nets of lines 27-99
ptw u_ptw (.*)      fe_tb_dut.svh:122  rtl/mmu/ptw/rtl/ptw.sv:155

What connects them, all by .* name matching:

translation group (itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2)
  tb nets fe_tb_dut.svh:45-61 and 106-107
  dut.itlb_l2t_*  (fe_top.sv:143-151)  -> u_ptw ports ptw.sv:170-178
  u_ptw.l2t_itlb_* (ptw.sv:179-188)   -> dut ports fe_top.sv:152-161
walker memory port (planning/interfaces/ptw_mem_interfaces.md 3)
  tb nets fe_tb_dut.svh:108-116
  u_ptw.ptw_mem_req_* (ptw.sv:191-196) -> memory model
  memory model -> u_ptw.mem_ptw_rsp_* (ptw.sv:197-199)
  model: fe_tb_mem.svh:106-226 (initial ptw_mem at 155; ready
  pattern at 224)
walker CSR group (MMU-24a)
  ptw_csr  fe_tb_dut.svh:117 -> u_ptw.ptw_csr ptw.sv:206
  driven by csr_sync, fe_tb_csr.svh:29 (csr_tb_pkg::pack_ptw_csr)
the L1I mem link (section 4.8)
  answered by the same memory model, fe_tb_mem.svh:35-103
  (a_ready at 35, the D-channel responder initial tl_mem at 37)

The walker and the L1I read one memory image (fe_tb_mem.svh; FE-21, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1490, ptw_mem_interfaces.md WM-10, line 143). fe_csr and ptw_csr are packed from the one csr_tb_pkg shadow (fe_tb_dut.svh:119-121).

docs.title: 8. Disagreements between the RTL and the planning documents
docs.text:
The RTL is what sections 2 to 7 record.

D1  FTB update port count.
    RTL: 15 payload ports plus the valid (fe_top.sv:274-289;
    bp_cluster.sv:195-211). The comments fe_top.sv:69, fe_top.sv:273,
    bp_cluster.sv:194 and ftq.sv:200 say 14.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 says 15 (lines 883, 895-900; "This
    read 14"). The plan agrees with the ports; the four RTL comments
    are stale since BP-121 added ftb_upd_jmp_rvc_u0.

D2  ITTAGE update payload name.
    RTL: ittage_upd_inp_u0 (fe_top.sv:298; bp_cluster.sv:219-220;
    ftq port bound at fe_top.sv:568).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 table, line 885, "ittage_upd_inp".

D3  TAGE and ITTAGE queue status port names (TD#49).
    RTL: tage.sv:47-48 and ittage.sv:46-47 declare <p>_pq_not_full and
    <p>_uq_not_full; bp_cluster.sv:1945-1946 and 1968-1969 bind them;
    bp_cluster.sv:286-288 says TD#49 was applied by BP-132.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8, lines 947-956, says tage and
    ittage declare pq_not_full and upd_rdy without prefix and that
    TD#49 is not yet applied. The cluster boundary names (tage_upd_rdy,
    ittage_upd_rdy) agree with lines 938-939.

D4  uBTB update port at the cluster boundary.
    RTL: ubtb_upd_u0, ubtb_upd_t [NUM_PRED_SLOTS-1:0], 352 bits
    (bp_cluster.sv:186; fe_top.sv:292).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 (line 881) names only the predictor
    port upd_u0; no planning document names the boundary port.

D5  Observation outputs.
    RTL: ftq_full and ftq_empty are fe_top outputs (fe_top.sv:212-216).
    Plan: in no FE-17 or FE-20 group (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1445) and
    named by no interface document.

D6  Decode outputs.
    RTL: decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle, is_vector, pd_out,
    vtype_hazard (fe_top.sv:103-107), from u_dec (fe_top.sv:820-824).
    Plan: FE-17 backend (fe_decisions.md:1410) says "decode to rename
    and dispatch" with no port list; no interface document names
    decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle or pd_out (is_vector and
    vtype_hazard appear in dcd_decisions.md:612 and 262).

D7  The instruction group.
    RTL: fe_top.sv:30-32 lists "instruction" as a boundary group, the
    20 l1i_mem_* ports (fe_top.sv:167-186).
    Plan: FE-17 (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1385) counts two groups and
    says the instruction path is not a boundary group, its `mem` port
    being a topology edge; FE-21 (fe_decisions.md:1479, 1490) says the
    port leaves the top as a boundary edge. The ports are the same;
    the documents count them differently.

D8  The config group comment.
    RTL: fe_top.sv:52-54 says "see Results Capture for the ones FE-20
    does not list".
    Plan: FE-20 config (fe_decisions.md:1459-1468) now lists every
    member fe_top distributes (sc_enable, ftb_fastpath_en, the four
    aging inputs, ext_enable); the comment refers to the text before
    the BP-118 correction.

D9  Walker-side labels.
    RTL: the server of the translation group is the page table walker
    (fe_tb_dut.svh:122; fe_top.sv:33-36).
    Plan: itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2 (lines 44-63) labels the far end
    "L2TLB" while its line 22 says the server is the walker. Naming
    only; ports and widths agree.

No width disagreement was found: every port width in ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 3 and 8, ftq_ifu_interfaces.md 4 to 6, l1i_ifu_interfaces.md 4.1, 5.1, 10.1 and 11.2, itlb_ifu_interfaces.md 2, ifu_ibuf_interfaces.md 2, ftq_backend_interfaces.md 4 to 6, itlb_l2tlb_interfaces.md 2 and ptw_mem_interfaces.md 3 that was compared resolves to the elaborated width recorded here.
